articles.headline: Russia will stop war if India halts oil buys: Zelensky
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged India, China, and Turkey to stop purchasing energy from Russia to end the ongoing war. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, he argued that Russia's economy relies on these countries to sustain its military operations. Zelensky claimed that stopping these sales would force Moscow to choose between its economy and its war efforts.

articles.headline: 10th seat sets up keen contest in U.P. RS elections
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha elections for 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh are poised for a significant contest. The BJP-led NDA has fielded eight candidates, while the SP-led Opposition has named three, despite being short of the required votes for a third seat. Both sides are actively seeking support from smaller parties, indicating a likelihood of cross-voting in the upcoming polls.

articles.headline: Monsoon leaves Delhi, earliest exit in 24 years
articles.summary: The southwest monsoon has withdrawn from Delhi on September 25, marking its earliest exit since 2002. This year's monsoon season in the capital lasted only 83 days, making it the shortest since 2012. Despite the early withdrawal, the city recorded 728.6mm of rainfall, which is 14% higher than the normal seasonal average. The withdrawal usually occurs around mid-October.

articles.headline: 4 in 10 Delhi homes not connected to sewage network
articles.summary: Around 40% of households in Delhi remain unconnected to the city's sewage network, according to Delhi Jal Board (DJB) data. This lack of infrastructure hampers efforts to meet the goal of cleaning the Yamuna River, as untreated waste continues to flow into the water body. Officials state that providing universal sewage coverage is essential to reducing pollution levels in the river.

articles.headline: Authors of error-riddled Odisha texts also tasked with reviewing
articles.summary: An inquiry into error-riddled school textbooks in Odisha revealed that the same individuals were assigned multiple roles as writers, reviewers, and proofreaders. The report highlighted 1,731 errors across 55 textbooks for Classes 1 to 8. These included factual errors in history and geography. The state has suspended several officials following findings of gross negligence and lack of oversight.

articles.headline: Domestic air passenger traffic falls for second month
articles.summary: Domestic air passenger traffic in India declined by 6.34% in August compared to the same period last year. Indian airlines carried 12.13 million passengers, down from 12.95 million in August 2023. This marks the second consecutive month of decline. High operating costs and a reduction in seasonal travel are cited as primary factors for the slowdown in the aviation sector.

articles.headline: 2 cops found dead in car in J&K’s Ramban
articles.summary: Two police officers, identified as Ahmed and Mohammad Yaqoob, were found dead inside a stationary car in Jammu and Kashmir's Ramban district. Authorities have ruled out foul play based on initial postmortem reports, suggesting the deaths were caused by suffocation or inhalation of toxic gases from the vehicle's air conditioning system. A detailed probe is underway to confirm the cause.

articles.headline: Centre cuts import duty on cooking oil
articles.summary: The Union government has significantly reduced basic customs import duties on crude soybean oil and crude palm oil to 5% from 10%. The total effective duty on refined sunflower oil has also been lowered to 12.5% from 32.5%. This move aims to stabilize domestic cooking oil prices, which have seen a sharp increase in recent months, providing relief to households during the festive season.

articles.headline: Gaza Board of Peace unveils $2.45bn fund
articles.summary: The Gaza Board of Peace, a US-backed initiative, announced a $2.45 billion reconstruction plan for the war-torn region. The fund aims to restore essential services, including housing, healthcare, and water infrastructure. The announcement comes nearly a year after the start of a ceasefire. The board plans to monitor the distribution of funds to ensure they are used for civilian welfare.

articles.headline: At heart of SIR controversy, ECI's software for officers
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) faces scrutiny over its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) software used in West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Delhi. Reports suggest the software flagged millions of voters for 'logical discrepancies,' potentially leading to disenfranchisement. Critics and opposition leaders have questioned the lack of transparency in the algorithm's criteria for voter deletion.

articles.headline: Expat killed, body dismembered in Sharjah; wife missing
articles.summary: A 55-year-old Indian man from Mangaluru was found dead in Sharjah, UAE. His body was dismembered and hidden in a suitcase. Local police discovered the body after family members in India lost contact with him. His wife and son, who were with him in Sharjah, are currently missing. UAE authorities have launched a manhunt and are coordinating with Indian officials to locate the family.

articles.headline: CM Shivakumar seeks 50% drought relief as interim aid
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM DK Shivakumar has urged the Central government to release 50% of the requested drought relief funds as interim aid. The state has sought ₹17,901 crore to compensate farmers for crop losses caused by a weak monsoon. Shivakumar stated that the situation in 216 out of 236 taluks is critical and immediate financial intervention is needed to support the rural economy.

articles.headline: Oppn plans motion to impeach CEC Kumar
articles.summary: Opposition parties in India are planning to move an impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Rajiv Kumar. The move comes amid allegations of bias and failure to act on complaints regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls. The Congress party claimed that the CEC's actions have compromised the integrity of the electoral process in several states.

articles.headline: Ayushman Bharat benefited 600mn since launch: Govt
articles.summary: The Union health ministry announced that the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) has benefited over 600 million people since its launch eight years ago. The world's largest health insurance scheme provides a cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care. PM Narendra Modi stated that the scheme has saved crores of families from medical debt.

articles.headline: India seeks more balanced trade in China ties
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal emphasized the need for a more balanced and sustainable trade relationship with China. Speaking at an event, he called for predictable market access for Indian products, especially in the pharma and IT sectors. While trade volume remains high, Agrawal noted that India's trade deficit with China continues to be a major concern for the government.

articles.headline: Iran calls out Trump at UNGA over sanctions
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian used his speech at the UN General Assembly to condemn Donald Trump's past actions and current rhetoric. He vowed that Iran would 'fight until our last breath' against external aggression and economic sanctions. Pezeshkian criticized the US for withdrawing from the nuclear deal and accused it of hindering regional peace through its support for Israel.

articles.headline: FBI hacked, data of thousands of employees stolen
articles.summary: The FBI is investigating a major cyberattack where hackers managed to steal sensitive data belonging to thousands of employees. A group known as 'ShinyHunters' claimed responsibility for the breach, which includes personal details and contact information. The FBI stated that it is working to mitigate the impact and identify the perpetrators. The incident raises concerns about national security.

articles.headline: The two-horse AI talent race between US and China
articles.summary: New research shows that the global race for top-tier AI researchers is largely a competition between the US and China. While the US currently leads in employing global talent, China has made significant strides in producing and retaining home-grown researchers. India produces around 4% of the world's elite AI talent but faces challenges in retaining them due to better opportunities abroad.

articles.headline: RBI approves record ₹2.11 lakh crore dividend transfer to Union Government
articles.summary: The RBI board approved a record ₹2.11 trillion surplus transfer to the government for the 2023-24 fiscal year. This amount is double the government's budgeted estimate of ₹1.02 trillion. The windfall is expected to help the Centre maintain its fiscal deficit target of 5.1% of GDP and potentially increase capital expenditure for the upcoming year.

articles.headline: UK annual inflation falls to 2.3% in April, lowest since 2021
articles.summary: UK inflation slowed to 2.3% in April, the lowest level in nearly three years, primarily due to falling domestic energy prices. While moving closer to the Bank of England's 2% target, the rate was slightly higher than the 2.1% forecasted by economists. This has led to market speculation that the central bank might wait until August or later to cut interest rates.

articles.headline: Government plans 5-10% hike in Minimum Support Price for Kharif crops
articles.summary: The Centre is considering an increase of 5-10% in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for Kharif crops for the 2024-25 season. The hike aims to support farmers against rising input costs and encourage the production of pulses and oilseeds. The decision is expected to be finalized soon to provide clarity to farmers before the onset of the monsoon sowing period.

articles.headline: SEBI mandates rumor verification for top 100 listed companies from June
articles.summary: SEBI has introduced new regulations requiring India's top 100 listed companies to verify market rumors within 24 hours of significant stock price movements. The rule, effective from June 1, aims to prevent speculation and protect investors from volatility caused by unverified news. The mandate will extend to the top 250 companies by the end of the year.

articles.headline: Titan Company announces ₹3,000 crore capital expenditure for retail expansion
articles.summary: Titan Company plans to invest ₹3,000 crore in FY25 to expand its retail footprint and manufacturing capabilities. The investment will primarily target the jewelry segment under Tanishq and the watches division. The company aims to leverage strong consumer demand and increase its presence in both metro and tier-2 cities, along with international store launches.

articles.headline: BharatPe reports 25% growth in annual revenue for fiscal year 2024
articles.summary: Fintech major BharatPe announced a 25% increase in its consolidated revenue for the 2023-24 fiscal year. The growth was driven by its core lending and merchant payments segments. The company reported a significant reduction in its burn rate and stated it is on track to achieve full-year Ebitda profitability, marking a key milestone in its turnaround strategy.

articles.headline: Adani Ports receives approval to expand Kattupalli port handling capacity
articles.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone has received environmental clearance to expand its Kattupalli port capacity. The project involves developing new berths and increasing cargo handling infrastructure. This expansion is part of the company's strategy to strengthen its logistics presence on India's eastern coast and meet growing trade demand.

articles.headline: ITC fourth quarter earnings to be driven by cigarette volume growth
articles.summary: ITC is expected to report a steady performance for the fourth quarter, with analysts projecting cigarette volume growth of 2-3%. The diversified conglomerate's FMCG and hotels divisions are also anticipated to show healthy margins. Market focus remains on the company's agribusiness segment and the ongoing demerger process of its hotels business.

articles.headline: Crude oil prices slip on expectations of higher US interest rates
articles.summary: Brent crude futures fell below $82 a barrel as concerns grew that persistent US inflation would lead to higher interest rates for longer, curbing global demand. Market participants are also awaiting the upcoming OPEC+ meeting in June for further direction on production cuts and supply levels for the second half of the year.

articles.headline: Kolkata Knight Riders beat Sunrisers Hyderabad to enter IPL 2024 final
articles.summary: Kolkata Knight Riders became the first team to reach the IPL 2024 final after an eight-wicket win over Sunrisers Hyderabad in Qualifier 1. Mitchell Starc's opening spell restricted SRH to 159, which KKR chased down comfortably in 13.4 overs. Venkatesh Iyer and Shreyas Iyer both scored unbeaten half-centuries to secure the victory in Ahmedabad.

articles.headline: Nayara-SAP order impact on Indian companies facing foreign sanctions
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court ordered SAP India to restore services to Nayara Energy, suspended due to EU sanctions over its Russian links. The ruling, based on Indian law governing contracts between Indian entities, offers potential relief to domestic companies facing foreign sanctions but is not immunity from them.

articles.headline: India leads EM peers in August but risks loom
articles.summary: India topped Mint's Emerging Markets Tracker in August due to strong GDP growth (7.8%), robust exports (26%), and rising import cover. However, it lagged peers on inflation (4.8%), currency, and stock market performance. Looming risks include a rate-hike cycle, rising US yields, West Asia war, and deficient monsoon rainfall impacting food prices and FPI outflows.

articles.headline: Brookfield’s Avaada bet doubles returns as company repays debt
articles.summary: Brookfield Renewable exited Avaada Ventures, realizing ₹6,713 crore (double its ₹3,290 crore investment) as Avaada repaid its debt. This exit precedes Avaada Electro Ltd's ₹7,600 crore IPO. Avaada, diversified in renewable energy and components, aims to use ₹1,200 crore from its fresh issue for debt repayment.

articles.headline: MacBook Neo sales shine for Apple in grim laptop market
articles.summary: Apple's MacBook Neo sales are surging in India, closing in on one million units annually, despite a double-digit decline in the overall laptop market. Apple's market share is projected to reach 7% this year, up from under 4% in 2025, driven by conservative price increases and the MacBook Neo's competitive pricing.

articles.headline: Sebi board expansion lacks key safeguard, experts say
articles.summary: India's proposed Securities Markets Code, 2025, expands SEBI's board from nine to 15 members but lacks an independent selection process for appointments. Experts warn this omission, unlike CERC and CCI laws, jeopardizes regulatory independence and transparency, as the process is left to rules rather than enshrined in law.

articles.headline: Irdai moots sweeping reset for insurance distribution
articles.summary: Irdai proposed major reforms for insurance distribution, including tighter Expense of Management (EoM) limits, product-level commission caps, and a ban on compulsory loan bundling. The overhaul aims to reduce costs, simplify regulation, and give policyholders greater choice, with insurers facing lower long-term targets.

articles.headline: India tightens warning labels for packaged food items
articles.summary: The FSSAI tightened proposed warning labels for packaged food, making them applicable if even one nutrient (salt, sugar, or fat) is high. The rollout will now occur in a single phase, affecting packaged products across India.

articles.headline: Govt cuts customs duty on edible oils ahead of festive season
articles.summary: The government cut basic customs duty (BCD) on crude soya bean and palm oils from 10% to 5%, and on refined variants from 32.5% to 27.5%. BCD on crude sunflower oil became nil, and on refined, it was reduced from 32.5% to 22.5%, ahead of the festive season.

articles.headline: Wholesale-retail pharmacy ratio planned to curb misuse of licences
articles.summary: The Union government plans to review drug licensing, proposing an indicative wholesale-to-retail pharmacy ratio based on population, disease burden, and existing licence density. This aims to bring uniformity across states and curb the misuse of wholesale licences for retail sales, which is not currently regulated by numerical limits.

articles.headline: Synechron holds talks with PE investors for stake sale
articles.summary: Synechron, a bootstrapped global IT company with over $1 billion in annual revenue, is discussing a stake sale with private equity firms like EQT AB, CVC, and Apax Partners. The proposed transaction could involve a minority or significant majority stake, with the company eyeing a valuation of $3-3.5 billion or more.

articles.headline: Ad margin key to Meesho profit amidst rising competition
articles.summary: Meesho's stock surged on strong Net Merchandise Value (NMV) growth (34% YoY in Q1FY27). Advertising contribution margin is key to achieving adjusted Ebitda profitability, which was negative 1.2% in Q1FY27. The zero-commission model faces growing competition from Amazon Bazaar and Flipkart Shopsy.

articles.headline: GE Vernova’s order book faces revenue conversion test
articles.summary: GE Vernova T&D India faces the challenge of converting its substantial ₹33,430 crore order backlog, nearly five times its FY26 revenue, into actual revenue. Large projects like the Barmer HVDC-LCC are expected to take about 4.5 years to execute, requiring efficient project management and execution capabilities.

articles.headline: Tata Tech’s China unit steps up battery work for Agratas
articles.summary: Tata Technologies' Shanghai unit is intensifying its support for Agratas Energy Storage Solutions, Tata group's battery venture, for lithium-ion battery development and deployment. This collaboration, along with a technology partnership with AESC, highlights Agratas's reliance on Chinese supply chains amid tech transfer restrictions.

articles.headline: Mediratta eyes 100 stores for grocery venture FreshTerra
articles.summary: Former Metro Cash & Carry India chief Arvind Mediratta's two-month-old grocery venture, FreshTerra, plans to expand to 100 stores, focusing on a store-first omnichannel model with own brands. The company expects to raise fresh capital within six months for store expansion, technology, and supply chain operations.

articles.headline: Supernova in talks to raise $15-20 mn for AI-powered English app
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based Supernova, an AI-powered app for learning spoken English, is in advanced talks to raise $15-20 million. The startup, with $15 million in annual recurring revenue, is in discussions with Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia and India, and Verlinvest, for the funding round.

articles.headline: Transport, mfg firms now lead India’s GCC boom
articles.summary: Manufacturing and transport companies now drive India's global capability centre (GCC) expansion, accounting for one in three new tech centers this year (30%). This surpasses BFSI firms' share (5.4%) and reflects industrial players' push for greater tech ownership and access to India's engineering talent in the AI era.

articles.headline: Chandra repayment plan: NCLT seeks CBI response
articles.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) sought a CBI response within four weeks regarding Zee founder Subhash Chandra's repayment plan for loans. The CBI is investigating allegations of cheating and criminal conspiracy related to ₹980 crore loans from LIC Housing Finance Ltd, for which Chandra provided personal guarantees.

articles.headline: Duty-free shops cannot claim exemption from Indian laws
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court ruled that airport duty-free shops are not exempt from Indian laws, including the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, despite operating beyond customs barriers. This decision came on a plea regarding the sale of tobacco-free nicotine pouches, affirming regulatory authority over such establishments.

articles.headline: PE firm Multiples targeting industrials as an investment frontier
articles.summary: Private equity firm Multiples Alternate Asset Management is expanding its investment focus to industrials, including precision manufacturing and defence. This shift is driven by diversifying global supply chains and a growing number of family-run businesses seeking scale, professionalization, and capital infusion.

articles.headline: How clock towers changed our rhythm and city identity
articles.summary: Clock towers, originally symbols of British imperial authority and precision timekeeping, became integral to India's civic life, shaping how towns worked and traded. Rising above public spaces, they synchronized daily rhythms, and many are now being restored, reflecting their historical and architectural significance.

articles.headline: Timid police film 'Daayra' refuses to get messy
articles.summary: Meghna Gulzar's film 'Daayra,' based on the 2019 Hyderabad rape case, explores an encounter killing by police but avoids moral complexities. Critics find the film's portrayal of 'virtuous' cops and tentative investigation leaves little room for viewer deliberation, aligning with similar recent Hindi films that lionize fascist justice.

articles.headline: John Wilson carves out a micro-movie revolution
articles.summary: Filmmaker John Wilson is creating an 'idiosyncratic micro-movie revolution' with his documentary style, capturing mundane realities and establishing the 42-seat Low Cinema in New York. His feature debut, 'The History of Concrete,' grossed $90,000, proving that authentic, personal art can thrive outside Hollywood blockbusters.

articles.headline: Kotak Alts raises ₹5,000 crore fund for private credit, assets
articles.summary: Kotak Alternate Asset Managers closed its Kotak Yield & Growth Fund (KYGF) at ₹5,000 crore, raised entirely from domestic institutional investors, family offices, and UHNIs. The fund will deploy capital across private credit, real assets, and selective growth opportunities in cash-flow-generating businesses.

articles.headline: Modi plans Canada trip for deal, speeds up Mexico talks
articles.summary: India is accelerating trade talks with Canada (deal likely in December during PM Modi's visit) and Mexico as all three economies seek new markets. This is in response to disruptions from US President Donald Trump’s tariff policies, aiming to diversify commercial ties and counter fresh tariff threats from a new US law.

articles.headline: From Wipro to ageing: Soota’s unfinished game
articles.summary: Ashok Soota, 83, a serial entrepreneur who built Mindtree and Happiest Minds to public listings, has sold his stake in Happiest Minds for ₹1,329.7 crore. He is now funding a new focus on human longevity, clinical care, and medical research through Happiest Health and his non-profit SKAN Research Trust, challenging conventional retirement paths.

articles.headline: Montessori to Waldorf: an early start with a steep bill
articles.summary: Pedagogy-based preschools (Montessori, Waldorf, Reggio Emilia) in Indian metros charge ₹2.5-4 lakh annually, significantly higher than regular preschools. While aiming for developmental benefits, parents must weigh these costs against their household finances and longer-term education goals to ensure sustainability.

articles.headline: Should you cut equity exposure as your retirement approaches?
articles.summary: As retirement nears, gradually shift funds from equity to more stable assets, rather than using a fixed age-based reduction. This approach aligns investments with the goal's time horizon. Regularly review goals and portfolio, adjusting for inflation, lifestyle changes, and financial responsibilities, while increasing investments as income grows.

articles.headline: Small-caps moved up market-cap ladder, risks remain
articles.summary: Small-caps have matured, with the entry threshold doubling to ₹33,500 crore and firms showing greater financial strength. They offer exposure to emerging businesses and delivered stronger long-term returns (Nifty Smallcap 250: 16% CAGR over 5 years). However, investors must brace for deeper, longer periods of volatility.

articles.headline: The ‘hold’ rating for securities: why it exists?
articles.summary: The 'hold' rating in securities analysis is economically irrational, stemming from endowment bias—an overvaluation of what one owns. This bias leads investors to hold stocks beyond rational valuation thresholds, often to avoid acknowledging past incorrect decisions or to achieve an irrational premium to sell, hindering optimal portfolio management.

articles.headline: India’s playing field for businesses: is it uneven?
articles.summary: India's complex regulatory environment, a legacy of the Licence Raj, continues to create an uneven playing field for businesses. Policy tools often favor key players, leading to abrupt rule tweaks and policy puzzles that deter foreign investors and compromise global corporate governance norms, despite India's economic potential.

articles.headline: Climate fight: recalibration may work, inaction won’t
articles.summary: Global warming's escalating impacts demand urgent action. While green transition financing is challenging, diverting development funds to climate policy at the expense of health and education for poor countries is misguided. A strategic recalibration is needed, including re-evaluating India's high import duties on solar panels, to quicken domestic change.

articles.headline: Deferred customs duty payment can make India more competitive
articles.summary: India's customs regime should shift to a default deferred payment system for all registered importers, moving away from requiring duty payment before cargo clearance. This reform would streamline supply chains, reduce costs, ease port congestion, and enhance India's attractiveness as an investment destination, trusting taxpayers based on their compliance records.

articles.headline: American press takes stand against Trump’s bullying tactics
articles.summary: The American press, including CNN, MS Now, and Politico, filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration for banning them from the White House, asserting First Amendment rights. They are also collectively refusing coverage of Trump's events, demonstrating solidarity against his bullying tactics and transparent efforts to control the narrative.

articles.headline: Who really benefits from fear-mongering around AI?
articles.summary: The article questions the intent behind AI leaders' public 'fear-mongering' about AI's destructive potential. It suggests this 'meta-talk' might be a strategic manipulation to highlight AI's power, secure public listings, and position firms as humanity's saviors, reminiscent of past PR playbooks used to promote new technologies while downplaying risks.

articles.headline: Meta to unveil new smart glasses including camera-free model
articles.summary: Meta, led by Zuckerberg, is set to unveil new smart glasses, including a camera-free model, amidst growing concerns over non-consensual recording and AI data privacy. This move comes as tech companies navigate the complexities of integrating advanced features with user privacy.

articles.headline: Udupi man’s body cut into 9 pieces in UAE; wife, son missing
articles.summary: The family of Alwin Prakash Kunder, a Udupi man allegedly murdered in the UAE, whose body was found cut into nine pieces, has sought a probe. His wife and teenage son are untraceable, raising suspicion and prompting a police investigation.

articles.headline: Karnataka drafts law to keep teachers off other duties
articles.summary: Karnataka government has drafted new legislation to restrict the deployment of government and aided school teachers for non-academic duties like polls and census work. The aim is to curb learning loss and ensure teachers' uninterrupted presence in classrooms.

articles.headline: MLA quits after 2 taluks don’t make drought list
articles.summary: Congress MLA Yashvanthraygoud V Patil submitted his resignation, protesting the exclusion of Indi and Chadachan taluks from the drought-hit list in Vijayapura district. This is his second resignation attempt this year, highlighting political embarrassment for the government.

articles.headline: LoP’s presence in panel to pick CEC, ECs ‘ornamental’: SC judge
articles.summary: Justice Dipankar Datta pointed out drawbacks in the law on appointing chief election commissioner and election commissioners, stating it gives "overwhelming" power to the executive and makes the LoP's presence "ornamental," undermining independence.

articles.headline: Deep depression batters Odisha, more rain expected
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal battered south Odisha, causing heavy rain, inundation, and landslides. More heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast, prompting the state government to deploy ODRAF teams and evacuate over 5,000 people.

articles.headline: Elected J&K govt has no say in book ban, says CM Omar
articles.summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah stated his elected government has no role in deciding which books are banned or withdrawn from libraries, distancing his administration from the removal of 4,249 books after a screening across the Union territory.

articles.headline: Illegal house demolition akin to ‘Brahma hatya’: HC
articles.summary: The Patna High Court ruled that illegal house demolition amounts to 'Brahma hatya,' upholding citizens' right to housing. It ordered compensation for villagers whose homes were razed by a mob in the presence of authorities, who remained "mute spectators."

articles.headline: Zelensky calls on India, China, Turkiye to halt energy trade with Russia
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky urged India, China, and Turkiye to halt their energy trade with Russia. He stated that stopping these fuel purchases would quickly end the war, as Moscow relies on these countries to sustain its economy and war efforts.

articles.headline: Mirabai Chanu bags India’s first weightlifting medal in 28 years
articles.summary: Mirabai Chanu bagged a silver medal in weightlifting, her first Asiad medal and India's first in the event in nearly three decades. Karnam Malleshwari last won silver at Bangkok in 1998, marking a significant return for Indian weightlifting.

articles.headline: Indian national killed in vessel attack off Oman
articles.summary: An Indian sailor, Suraj Yadav, was killed in an attack on a commercial vessel off the east coast of Oman. 19 other Indian seafarers were rescued. India condemned the attack, calling continuing incidents on ships deeply worrisome.

articles.headline: Jaishankar brings up curbs, Rubio harps on friendship
articles.summary: EAM S Jaishankar raised India's concerns over Washington's Russia sanctions law with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, exposing a rift. Jaishankar's post was specific, mentioning sanctions, while Rubio's post on X made no reference to it, highlighting differing priorities.

articles.headline: Karnataka registered births cross 10 lakh, rural non-institutional births rise
articles.summary: Karnataka's registered births crossed 10 lakh in 2025, but the state's birth rate dropped 30% in 25 years. The share of non-institutional rural births rose significantly from 80.2% in 2021 to 53.2% in 2025, signaling a decline in healthcare access.

articles.headline: Man duped of `54,000 in fancy number fraud
articles.summary: A 56-year-old Bengaluru businessman was duped of Rs 54,000 after a fraudster posed as a seller of fancy mobile numbers over WhatsApp. The victim shared KYC details and OTPs, but the SIM cards were never activated, leading to a police complaint.

articles.headline: Open schooling to see revamp with on-demand exams
articles.summary: Karnataka plans to revamp its open schooling system, introducing on-demand exams and curriculum aligned with SSLC and II PU. The new rules allow credit transfer from other boards and flexible subject choices, aiming to provide alternatives for out-of-school learners.

articles.headline: 160 Bangladeshi nationals deported from Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru deported 160 Bangladeshi nationals found staying illegally during a special drive. The city police coordinated with FRRO, BSF, and IAF for a special flight from HAL airport to repatriate the individuals, marking the second such large-scale deportation.

articles.headline: Work on business park at KIA to start soon
articles.summary: Civil work for a major part of the 2.2 million-sqft business park around Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) is expected to kick off soon. Construction is underway on 7.9 acres for the first block, with an urban forest corridor also being built.

articles.headline: Cop on duty, burglars strike at his home
articles.summary: A head constable from Yelahanka New Town police station returned home after duty to find burglars had broken into his rented residence, fleeing with 35 grams of gold jewellery and Rs 6,000 cash. His wife and son were away caring for her ailing father.

articles.headline: Drunk girl bites home guard during crowd rescue
articles.summary: A 19-year-old girl, Sara Vijay, driving under the influence, hit a Ganesha immersion procession near Orion Avenue Mall, injuring participants. When police intervened to protect her from an angry crowd, she abused, assaulted, and bit a woman home guard.

articles.headline: Karnataka to have advanced lab soon to test drugs
articles.summary: Karnataka will soon set up a high-quality laboratory to obtain scientifically robust drug test reports, aiming to strengthen drug-testing infrastructure. Health minister UT Khader also requested the Centre to bring serious drug-related offenses under stronger criminal provisions.

articles.headline: 6 lakh voters seek inclusion as objection time ends
articles.summary: Over 6 lakh voters have applied for inclusion in the final electoral rolls through Form 6 during the special intensive revision (SIR) period. Officials from the chief electoral officer's office stated that claims and objections will be considered for the Oct 27 rolls.

articles.headline: FDA seeks price cap on essential medical devices
articles.summary: Karnataka's Food Safety and Drugs Administration (FDA) urged the Centre to regulate prices of essential medical devices, proposing a National List of Essential Medical Devices (NLEMD). This move aims to reduce patients' out-of-pocket expenditure amid pricing controversies.

articles.headline: Compassionate ground can’t be used to seek higher posts: HC
articles.summary: The Dharwad bench of Karnataka High Court ruled that compassionate appointments are a one-time measure for immediate financial assistance and cannot be a recurring claim for higher posts or better service benefits. It reversed KSAT orders for two individuals seeking FDA appointments.

articles.headline: Teachers protected from punitive action for refusing non-academic duties
articles.summary: New draft legislation protects government schoolteachers from disciplinary action if they refuse non-educational work that violates the Act's provisions. It mandates that no school or classroom should be without instruction and lost teaching hours must be restored within 30 days.

articles.headline: BEML trainsets for Pink Line section cleared
articles.summary: BMRCL received railway board's sanction for new BEML trainsets to be deployed on the elevated section of the Pink Line. This is a key requirement for commissioning the 7-km stretch, with CMRS inspection expected in the first week of October.

articles.headline: HC bins plea of Darshan’s wife challenging approver status
articles.summary: The high court rejected a petition by jailed actor Darshan’s wife, Vijayalakshmi, challenging a trial court order granting approver status to an accused in the Renukaswamy murder case. The court noted the approver is yet to be examined and cross-examined.

articles.headline: Bengaluru doctor develops new shoulder surgery technique
articles.summary: Dr. Banarji BH developed a patented transosseous repair technique for rotator cuff repair, eliminating suture anchors. This method, suitable for patients with weak bones, involves creating tunnels through the bone to reattach the tendon, potentially reducing surgery costs by 25-30%.

articles.headline: Drought debate turns into argument over lack of Union govt funds
articles.summary: The special legislative session on drought turned into a political confrontation, with opposition BJP and JD(S) targeting the government over its handling of the crisis and lack of Central assistance. The debate was repeatedly disrupted by sharp exchanges and walkouts.

articles.headline: Minister scrambles to clarify graft remark, insists no one needs to pay `10
articles.summary: Excise minister KM Shivalingegowda insisted he only asked people to treat government officials respectfully after work completion, not to pay bribes. This followed accusations of promoting bribery when he told people to 'respectfully pay' officials, leading to a Lokayukta complaint.

articles.headline: Partyman accuses edu min’s aides of collecting bribes
articles.summary: Shivamogga Urban Development Authority (SUDA) chairman HS Sundaresh accused education minister Madhu Bangarappa’s aides of demanding money from officials. He warned CM DK Shivakumar of mass resignations if issues are not resolved within a month, also questioning Madhu’s credentials.

articles.headline: Victim’s kin get death cert, but not FIR copy
articles.summary: The family of Alwin Prakash Kunder, allegedly murdered in UAE, received his death certificate but not the FIR copy. They are unable to contact his wife and son, claiming CCTV footage showed two men and a woman moving luggage from their apartment.

articles.headline: MLA was concerned about farmers: CM
articles.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar stated MLA Yashvanthraygoud V Patil’s resignation was driven by concern for farmers, adding that drought declaration follows specific guidelines for central relief. This followed Patil's repeated requests for drought status for Indi and Chadachan taluks.

articles.headline: 75,000 VTU students to get degrees
articles.summary: Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) will hold its 26th annual convocation, with over 75,000 students set to receive degrees. Three eminent educationists will be conferred honorary doctorates during the event, presided over by Governor Thaawar Chand Gehlot.

articles.headline: EC clarifies faultlines: internal notes are normal practice
articles.summary: The Election Commission stated that 'differing views and observations' are a normal part of deliberation, after reports highlighted faultlines among commissioners. It clarified that written notes, suggestions, and internal checks are standard practices to ensure transparency and legal compliance.

articles.headline: Allegations of transfer of BCI assets to trust matter of concern: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court expressed concern over allegations of Bar Council of India's assets being transferred to a trust created by its chairperson. The court will examine BCI's power to establish and regulate law colleges and universities, seeking a response within two weeks.

articles.headline: Conversion doesn’t end ST status: Allahabad HC
articles.summary: Allahabad HC ruled that conversion to another religion does not, by itself, end Scheduled Tribe (ST) status. However, it dismissed a woman’s plea related to land purchase, as she failed to establish retention of her tribal identity after marriage and conversion.

articles.headline: Rahul accuses BJP, RSS, EC of treason over 'vote chori'
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi accused BJP, RSS, and EC of 'treason' over alleged 'vote chori', calling it a direct attack on the Constitution. Opposition leaders demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar's arrest and a probe, citing reports of dissenting ECs and widespread voter deletions.

articles.headline: BJP defends EC, says opposition trying to discredit panel
articles.summary: BJP defended the Election Commission, stating differences of opinion within EC are a sign of democratic functioning. It accused the opposition of trying to discredit institutions since 2014 due to dwindling popular support, calling their outrage an outcome of receding influence.

articles.headline: Student stabbed at busy Kol mall
articles.summary: A 20-year-old engineering student was arrested for allegedly stabbing his classmate and slashing his neck inside a Kolkata shopping mall. The victim is battling for life, and police suspect a quarrel over a girl triggered the attack.

articles.headline: Bangladesh cancels hilsa permits
articles.summary: Bangladesh cancelled import permits for hilsa, halting a trade that saw 550 tonnes of Indian hilsa enter the country. Sources indicate the suspension followed a meeting, raising concerns for India's festival season hilsa exports amid record low catches in Bangladesh.

articles.headline: SHO shunted for ‘Naagin dance’
articles.summary: The SHO of Rampura in UP’s Jalaun district was shunted to police lines for allegedly forcing a BJP functionary to perform a "naagin dance" at his police station. The BJP functionary had complained of extortion demands by the SHO.

articles.headline: Cannot direct Speaker but expect early ruling on TMC rebels: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court remarked it cannot direct the Lok Sabha Speaker but expects an "expeditious" decision on a plea seeking disqualification of 20 rebel TMC MPs. The court reminded the Speaker of the seriousness of the matter, urging quick resolution.

articles.headline: Bhopal Class X girl bags perfect score after CBSE re-evaluation
articles.summary: A Class 10 girl in Bhopal secured a perfect score of 500 after CBSE re-evaluated her marks. Nandika Gupta had challenged two answers wrongly marked incorrect, leading CBSE to acknowledge its error in the answer key and award her additional marks.

articles.headline: IIT-B student’s kin claim they were driven out of city
articles.summary: The parents of IIT-B student Sahil Wakode alleged they were driven out of Mumbai in a "private car" despite wanting to stay and begin a hunger strike. They claimed police vehicles followed their car before it entered the Samruddhi Expressway.

articles.headline: Raj HC orders Cong woman to share salary with mom-in-law
articles.summary: Rajasthan HC ordered Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (AVVNL) to deduct 25% of a woman employee’s salary, received for a compassionate job, and transfer it to her mother-in-law for her lifetime. This ruling provides financial support to the bereaved mother-in-law.

articles.headline: Nandigram pick sent to jail in new case, to stay in custody till bypoll
articles.summary: A court remanded Congress’ Nandigram bypoll candidate, Milan Pradhan, to judicial custody until Oct 7 in a new criminal case. His legal team moved Calcutta High Court, alleging the order came despite assurance that no other cases were pending against him.

articles.headline: Autopsy confirms Koli died by hanging; police probe circumstances
articles.summary: Postmortem confirmed Surendra Koli, found dead at his tea stall in Haridwar, died of ante-mortem hanging. Police are investigating the circumstances and examining call detail records, though CCTV footage has shown no suspicious activity around the stall.

articles.headline: Panchayat boycotts, fines family `1L over love marriage
articles.summary: A caste council in Maharashtra's Jalgaon district allegedly fined a family Rs 1 lakh and socially ostracised them after their daughter married a man from her own community without informing the council, violating customary rules.

articles.headline: Bengal govt to shut down another 250 unaided madrasas
articles.summary: Bengal's government plans to shut down around 250 more government-recognised unaided madrasas after December. This follows notices for immediate closure of 252 madrasas lacking minimum infrastructure, aiming for modern education for students.

articles.headline: 7,375 forest boundary pillars go missing in Mussoorie
articles.summary: Uttarakhand high court widened scrutiny into the disappearance of 7,375 forest boundary pillars in Mussoorie division, issuing notices to CBI, Centre, and state government. The PIL highlights large-scale disappearance and alleged disproportionate rise in assets of a supervising forest officer.

articles.headline: SC: Constitution bench should deal with EC appointment case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed that the long-pending case regarding the validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench. This decision aims to settle the significant issue once and for all, avoiding further delay and institutional embarrassment.

articles.headline: Delhi gang rape: Probe on if park was a hunting ground
articles.summary: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi are trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar unreported incidents. The accused allegedly posed as policemen to intimidate and assault the couple.

articles.headline: BJP appoints in-charges; Smriti Irani gets Chhattisgarh, Haryana
articles.summary: BJP appointed in-charges for its nationwide organisational functioning, naming Harish Dwivedi for Bihar and Karnataka, Smriti Irani for Chhattisgarh and Haryana, and Ram Madhav for Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. These key appointments will oversee party operations.

articles.headline: Student barred for not paying fee to take exams
articles.summary: MP high court ordered management of a private medical college to let an MBBS student take his third-semester exams, after he was barred for not depositing his fee. The court issued notices to state government and college authorities.

articles.headline: Seers, priests slam DJ music outside Badrinath shrine
articles.summary: A cultural event outside Badrinath shrine drew criticism from seers and temple priests over loud DJ music and dance performances near the sacred site. The two-day program, featuring folk singer Priyanka Meher, was attended by CM Pushkar Singh Dhami.

articles.headline: Patient dies, AIIMS doc thrashed in ICU
articles.summary: Police registered an FIR against four relatives of a 66-year-old patient following a complaint by a resident doctor at AIIMS-Nagpur. The doctor alleged verbal abuse and assault inside the ICU after the patient's death.

articles.headline: Another woman attacked in Gurgaon road rage
articles.summary: Weeks after a similar incident, another woman was attacked in Gurgaon. A Scorpio driver chased and rammed her car, abusing her and her mother, and smashing the car's headlight with an iron rod near AIT Chowk. Police registered an FIR after a month.

articles.headline: Trump’s Canadian immigration claims fail maths
articles.summary: Donald Trump claimed Canada is 'destroying itself' with 'millions and millions' of unchecked migrants, but official data shows Canada admits 483,000 permanent residents annually, focusing on economic programs, a figure far less than his claim and lower than US legal immigration.

articles.headline: Desi lawyer denied bail in UK sexual assault case
articles.summary: Indian lawyer Vijay Aggarwal was denied bail in the UK, accused of sexual assault and human trafficking. The judge cited a major flight risk, as Aggarwal has no strong UK ties and the allegations are serious, involving drawing young women into sexual wishes.

articles.headline: Rubio says Trump invited Putin for G20 meeting in Miami
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump has invited Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit in Miami in December. This move comes as Washington struggles to secure a deal to end Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

articles.headline: Zelensky urges world to keep choking Russia’s revenues
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged world leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues to impede its war efforts, stating that "Russia’s revenues must remain a target." He emphasized that more trade with Russia gives the war more time, calling for limiting trade with the aggressor.

articles.headline: UK to launch military space squadron to defend satellites
articles.summary: Britain announced it will launch a new military space squadron to defend the country’s satellites, as various nations rush for military space capabilities. The Royal Air Force squadron will protect critical satellites used in communications and missile attack warnings.

articles.headline: Judge to weigh Trump’s WH ban on media outlets
articles.summary: A US federal judge will consider a demand by CNN, MSNBC, and Politico to restore their White House access after President Trump revoked credentials. The media outlets argue the ban violates the First Amendment, seeking a temporary restraining order.

articles.headline: Archaeological breakthrough confirms origins of Paris
articles.summary: An ancient wall discovered beneath Paris was described as a "major breakthrough," possibly confirming the location of the city's original settlement. The 65-foot Gallo-Roman era wall, found beneath a hotel, bears traces of fire corresponding to Julius Caesar's account.

articles.headline: Nike founder, wife donate $1bn to Oregon University
articles.summary: Phil Knight, Nike Inc. founder, and his wife committed $1 billion to the University of Oregon, one of the largest donations ever to a public university. The gift will establish the Knight College of Engineering, marking their third large donation to the university.

articles.headline: Regional monetary policy remains cautious, with divergent paths ahead
articles.summary: Most central banks held rates in 2026, with hikes picking up in Q2 due to surging energy prices before pausing. Regional monetary policy remains cautious, with central banks taking divergent paths through the end of 2027.

articles.headline: Insurance commissions capped as fees soar 4x faster than premium
articles.summary: The insurance regulator sought to curb distribution costs and misselling by tightening limits on commissions and expenses. Irdai found distributor remuneration grew four to five times faster than gross premium, absorbing a larger share and reducing affordability.

articles.headline: Chandra’s real vote test: AGM, not boardroom
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as a director for Tata Sons depends on an upcoming shareholder vote, not just the board's decision. An earlier AGM was adjourned for lack of quorum. Trusts holding 42% of shares are expected to vote against.

articles.headline: Inflation to stay within band: RBI DG
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated India's inflation is likely to remain within the target band, unlike several advanced economies. She added there's scope for the rupee to appreciate and that India's growth was the highest among its peers.

articles.headline: JSW Greentech enters e-trucks business, aims 1 lakh units by 2030
articles.summary: Sajjan Jindal’s JSW Greentech is entering the commercial electric trucks business, aiming to sell one lakh units by 2030. The plant, soon operational, will have a capacity for 15,000 electric buses and trucks annually, with 3,000 electric trucks sales expected this year.

articles.headline: Ema raises $77mn to expand AI business
articles.summary: Enterprise AI startup Ema has raised $77 million in a funding round led by Creaegis, bringing its total funding to $140 million. Existing investors Accel, S32, and Prosus also increased their investments in the Bengaluru-based company.

articles.headline: Financial system needs to evolve: SBI chief
articles.summary: SBI chairman C S Setty stated India’s financial system needs to evolve to finance the country’s next phase of economic expansion. He emphasized banks playing a larger role in supporting higher-value manufacturing, new technologies, and the green transition.

articles.headline: Zoho steps up focus on vertical applications
articles.summary: Zoho will increase its focus on industry-specific, vertical applications, targeting seven sectors including auto and financial services. The company announced its entry into vertical applications, expecting each sector to offer $20 million opportunities, aiming for quicker implementations and new customers.

articles.headline: Milne, Bracewell return to New Zealand T20I squad
articles.summary: New Zealand fast bowler Adam Milne and spin all-rounder Michael Bracewell have returned to a 16-member squad for next month’s T20I home series against India. The duo's inclusion boosts the team's bowling and all-round options.

articles.headline: Akaash Ashok Kumar triumphs in state tenpin bowling
articles.summary: Akaash Ashok Kumar won the Karnataka State Ranking Tenpin Bowling Tournament in Bengaluru. He dominated the final against top seed Kishan R, winning by 101 pins across two games, securing the top spot.

articles.headline: KSCA to conduct selection trials for U-23 women’s cricket
articles.summary: KSCA will conduct open selection trials for Bangalore Zone cricketers to identify players for three/four teams participating in U-23 women’s selection matches next month. Girls born between Sept 1, 2003, and Aug 31, 2011, are eligible to participate.

articles.headline: Yu Zidi, 13, completes golden hat-trick in swimming
articles.summary: Chinese swimming sensation Yu Zidi, 13, capped her fairytale Asian Games debut with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, setting a new Games record. This completes her golden hat-trick, reaffirming her generational talent.

articles.headline: In Neeraj’s absence, eyes on Toor and Ancy for medals
articles.summary: With Neeraj Chopra out due to injury, India’s medal hopes at the Asian Games turn to athletes like Tajinderpal Singh Toor (shot put) and Ancy Sojan (long jump). Toor aims for a third successive Asian Games gold, while Sojan has established herself as a leading field athlete.

articles.headline: China avenge Oly defeat in gymnastics clash with Japan
articles.summary: Zhang Boheng led China to avenge their Olympic defeat to Japan in gymnastics, securing a third consecutive men’s team gold. The 26-year-old Hunan native delivered a crucial clean high bar routine on the final rotation to keep the continental gold in Chinese hands.

articles.headline: Khalid Jamil plans to catch Panama by surprise
articles.summary: India coach Khalid Jamil believes his side can catch visitors Panama by surprise in the upcoming FIFA friendly despite Panama's higher ranking. Jamil emphasizes playing attacking football and leveraging the home crowd's support for a good result.

articles.headline: BFC in cruise mode with 3-0 win
articles.summary: BFC eased to a 3-0 win over FC Agniputhra in the Karnataka Super Division League football championship in Bengaluru. The team's dominant performance secured a comfortable victory.

articles.headline: Khalin Joshi stays in lead at Bengaluru Open
articles.summary: Khalin Joshi maintained his lead at the Bengaluru Open, stretching it to six shots with a composed four-under 68. The Bengaluru golfer moved to 15-under 129 at the halfway stage, cheered on by a home crowd.

articles.headline: Emphatic for feature event in Mysuru racing
articles.summary: The James McKeown-trained Chitrangada and Emphatic, with Yash Narredu in the saddle, commands attention in The HH Sri Chamaraja Wadiyar Memorial Trophy, the feature event in Mysuru racing.

articles.headline: North Korea’s weightlifter Ri Song Gum breaks three world records
articles.summary: North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum broke three world records en route to winning her third Asian Games gold medal. The 28-year-old lifted 94kg in snatch and 121kg in clean-and-jerk, totaling 215kg, claiming gold in the women's 49kg category.

articles.headline: Private fuel retailers cap per transaction diesel sale
articles.summary: Private fuel retailers have started rationing diesel sales at their outlets, with caps ranging from 50 to 200 litres per transaction. This comes amid a surge in global crude prices and reports of commercial users purchasing large quantities, while state-owned companies have no restrictions.

articles.headline: TN bizman’s premises raided in child rape case
articles.summary: City police searched the residential and office premises of granite baron R Veeramani in connection with a child rape case, three weeks after his arrest. A lookout circular was also issued against his son, Prakash, for his role in suspicious financial transactions.

articles.headline: Jumbos binge on mahua, keeping forest fringe villages on brink
articles.summary: Over 40 elephants from two herds are moving through forest-fringe villages in Chhattisgarh, feeding on crops and entering settlements for mahua and rice. Families shift to rooftops for safety, as human-elephant conflict continues to challenge residents during crop season.

articles.headline: Female cheetah from Botswana makes first kill
articles.summary: Cheetah Radha, released into Madhya Pradesh’s Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary on Sept 20, made her first kill within days. Forest officers reported the roughly two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah successfully hunted on Tuesday, signaling a confident start to her new life.

articles.headline: 1,731 errors crept into textbooks in Odisha
articles.summary: Lack of writer orientation and one-day review for subject experts contributed to 1,731 errors in Odisha’s school textbooks. An inquiry found the same resource persons wrote, reviewed, and cleared the books, leading to criminal and disciplinary action against officials.

articles.headline: Kharif crop gone, rabi in doubt: Why Maha farmers distressed
articles.summary: Failed kharif season and prolonged rainfall deficit have left Maharashtra's farmers distressed. Water sources are shrinking, livestock are being sold cheap, and families are migrating early for work, leading to concerns about food, debt, and the next sowing season.

articles.headline: Ilaiyaraaja honored with Australian Parliament Stamp
articles.summary: Veteran music composer Ilaiyaraaja was honored with an Australian Parliament Stamp for his five-decade legacy in music. This recognition celebrates his significant contributions to the Indian music industry and his global impact.

articles.headline: Imtiaz Ali’s daughter Ida is engaged!
articles.summary: Imtiaz Ali's daughter Ida Ali got engaged to her longtime boyfriend Krish Agrawal, sharing pictures from an intimate ceremony. The filmmaker posted the news on Instagram, seeking blessings for the newly engaged couple, who have not yet announced wedding plans.

articles.headline: Anant Nag: ‘This award does not belong to me alone’
articles.summary: Veteran Kannada actor Anant Nag was honored with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the 72nd National Film Awards. He reflected on his acting career, acknowledging the contributions of directors, producers, and technicians, and dedicated the award to millions who connected with his characters.

articles.headline: Daisy Bopanna: ‘Enough money; not why I came back to films’
articles.summary: Daisy Bopanna, returning to Kannada cinema after a deliberate break, stated her comeback isn't for money or nostalgia. She aims for powerful, non-stereotypical roles, like the villain in MG Srinivas' upcoming Birbal Trilogy Case 2, drawn by the character's intensity and impact.

articles.headline: President Murmu urges artistes not to endorse harmful products
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu urged popular film artistes not to endorse products harmful to health, emphasizing their immense influence on youth. She also called for greater participation of women on juries for the National Film Awards, promoting inclusivity and diverse perspectives.

articles.headline: Garba partner for rent? Viral joke draws police, cyber scrutiny
articles.summary: A 'rent a garba partner' post went viral, intended as satire but sparking police warnings about financial fraud. Cyber Cell Inspector DV Gamit advised background checks for vulnerable youngsters seeking partners, emphasizing that such trends can lead to scams.

articles.headline: Acid attack survivors create art from passport photos
articles.summary: The 'Passport' project, a collaboration between artist Raghava KK and Ara Lumiere, features acid attack survivors creating art from digitally altered passport photographs. Presented at Milan Fashion Week, it explores identity beyond physical erasure, allowing women to express themselves as creators.

articles.headline: Bengaluru drag queens pay heartfelt tribute to Dolly Parton
articles.summary: Bengaluru's drag community honored Dolly Parton with a heartfelt tribute, with performers like Sylveria Frost, Izzy B, and Lilith drawing on different facets of her legacy. The tribute celebrated Dolly's glamour, spirit, and iconic status within the LGBTQIA+ community.

articles.headline: The ultimate British roll call at LFWW 2026
articles.summary: Burberry delivered a memorable grand finale to London Fashion Week for its Spring/Summer 2027 showcase. Celebrities like Jonathan Bailey, Joe Locke, Rosie Huntington-Whiteley, Jason Statham, Lila Moss, Romeo Beckham, and Stephen Graham attended.

articles.headline: Film Awards to get new address annually to promote tourism
articles.summary: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting plans to host future National Film Awards ceremonies outside Mumbai and Delhi, rotating annually to promote tourism. States will nominate destinations, with the strongest case selected to host the event and benefit from celebrity influence.

articles.headline: Mithya secures hat-trick for Kannada cinema at National Film Awards
articles.summary: Sumanth Bhat-directed Mithya brought three honors to Kannada cinema at the 72nd National Film Awards. The film won Best Kannada Feature Film, with Roopashree Varkady taking Best Supporting Actress and Athish S Shetty winning Best Child Artist.

articles.headline: Dhanush’s Raayan secures Best Tamil Film
articles.summary: Dhanush's directorial debut, Raayan, secured Best Tamil Film at the 72nd National Film Awards. He also received a Special Mention for his performance in Captain Miller, which won for Feature Film Promoting National, Social, and Environmental Values.

articles.headline: Randeep Hooda awarded Best Debut Director for Savarkar film
articles.summary: Randeep Hooda was awarded Best Debut Director for his 2024 directorial debut, Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. Hooda expressed an overwhelming feeling, calling the National Award a 'big pat on the back' and encouragement for more work as a director and actor.

articles.headline: Sukumar wins Best Screenplay Writer for Pushpa 2: The Rule
articles.summary: Sukumar won the Best Screenplay Writer award for Pushpa 2: The Rule (2024). Deepali Noor and Sheetal Sharma were also honored with Best Costume Designer for the film, celebrating their contributions to the cinematic achievement.

articles.headline: Govt sets riders for funds to 3 stressed PSU insurers
articles.summary: The Centre finalized a turnaround strategy for National Insurance, Oriental Insurance, and United India Insurance. Fresh equity support will be linked to performance improvements like underwriting overhaul, product innovation, and performance-linked talent management, not just capital infusion. The three insurers face significant losses and negative solvency ratios, raising financial stability concerns for RBI.

articles.headline: 2 in 5 overnight trips in rural India for medical care
articles.summary: According to an NSO survey, 38.4% of overnight trips by rural Indians are for medical care, more than double urban peers. These trips are the costliest, averaging ~29,454 for rural households, who spend 75% on treatment. Government reimbursements cover only 8.2% of costs, highlighting the financial burden on rural families.

articles.headline: Fuel shift gathers pace across vehicle segments
articles.summary: India's auto market sees a significant fuel shift, with EVs gaining ground in PVs, two-wheelers, and three-wheelers, while CNG strengthens in PVs. Petrol/ethanol's share in PV retail sales fell from 47.49% to 40.85% (Jan-Aug), while EV penetration more than doubled. CNG, hybrid, and EVs now account for 41.95% of PV retail.

articles.headline: NTPC, Adani to conduct nuclear power plant feasibility study in Odisha
articles.summary: Odisha granted in-principle approval to state-owned NTPC and private Adani Power for feasibility studies on nuclear power projects. NTPC selected a site near Deogarh, while Adani Power will examine sites near Balimela Dam and Manjore Dam. This marks Odisha's first step towards adding nuclear power.

articles.headline: Netradyne, govt discuss driver-monitoring systems for CVs
articles.summary: AI-powered fleet-safety firm Netradyne is in talks with MoRTH to mandate driver-monitoring systems for commercial vehicles (CVs) in India. A state-level pilot with transport buses and tourism taxis is planned. The company also seeks factory-level integration with CV manufacturers, aiming to significantly reduce road accidents through AI and computer vision.

articles.headline: Amazon Retail FY26 losses widen to ~1,158.3 crore
articles.summary: Amazon Retail, operating Amazon Now and Amazon Fresh, saw its net losses widen to ~1,158.3 crore in FY26, from ~394.2 crore in FY25. The significant increase was mainly due to a 64% rise in the cost of goods sold, reaching ~2,887.9 crore, which accounted for almost 94% of the company's revenue.

articles.headline: Delhi-bound IndiGo plane faces technical issue, returns to London
articles.summary: A Delhi-bound IndiGo Dreamliner (Boeing 787-9) operating flight 6E4 from London Heathrow returned to the airport shortly after takeoff due to a technical issue. The aircraft landed safely, according to sources and flight tracking data. The airline did not immediately provide further details.

articles.headline: Rado's India story clocks good times, now No. 1 market globally
articles.summary: Swiss watch brand Rado's India market has surpassed China to become its largest globally since 2023. CEO Adrian Bosshard credits India's young population, growing economy, and increasing luxury segment participation. Rado plans to expand its boutique distribution, focusing on quality and retail experience in Tier-I, Tier-II, and Tier-III cities.

articles.headline: Fujifilm India exploring deals to supply chemicals to domestic chip cos
articles.summary: Fujifilm India is exploring supply deals for chemicals and semiconductor raw materials with Indian chip manufacturers, including Tata Electronics. The company plans an ~800 crore investment for a new semiconductor materials facility in Dholera, targeting production by 2027-28 and aiming to partner with local suppliers for raw materials and technology transfer.

articles.headline: Zoho rolls out AI-based Zia Chat for frictionless work
articles.summary: Chennai-based Zoho launched Zia Chat, an AI interface designed to streamline workplace tasks by providing a single, unified AI interface across various applications. Zia Chat enables users to find information, understand context, and take action through one interface, reducing time spent navigating fragmented software. Zoho also announced its entry into vertical SaaS.

articles.headline: Mavenir, Neysa partner to offer sovereign AI infra to enterprises
articles.summary: US-based Mavenir and Mumbai-based Neysa partnered to help telcos, enterprises, and neocloud providers build and monetize AI infrastructure. Their combined stack will enable sovereign AI system deployment without needing to assemble technology or infrastructure, converting GPU capacity into AI services for on-premises or hybrid environments.

articles.headline: Syneos Health opens global tech centre in Hyderabad
articles.summary: Syneos Health, a biopharmaceutical company, opened its largest Asian facility in Hyderabad, a 137,000-sq-ft global life sciences and technology centre. This expands Hyderabad's hub, making it home to four of the top five Contract Research Organizations. The centre will initially employ over 700 professionals.

articles.headline: Chintan Shivir discusses Viksit Bharat priorities
articles.summary: A Chintan Shivir, chaired by PM Modi, convened the entire council of ministers to deliberate on government projects, future plans, and next-generation reforms towards Viksit Bharat@2047. Discussions focused on improving coordination, preparing future agendas, and reviewing ongoing work on welfare schemes and infrastructure. Another session is expected next week.

articles.headline: Jaishankar airs India’s concerns over new tariff Act with Rubio
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, reiterating India's concerns regarding the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), which authorizes up to 100% tariffs on countries buying Russian oil. India aims to protect its economic interests and ensure energy security amid geopolitical uncertainties.

articles.headline: German envoy urges deepening India defence ties
articles.summary: Germany's envoy to India, Jasper Wieck, stated that the finalized ~8 billion India-Germany submarine pact, awaiting India's internal processes, could deepen defense and security cooperation. Germany has eased export restrictions, seeing India as a trusted partner amid global strategic shifts. Wieck also aims to double India-EU bilateral trade within five years.

articles.headline: Farm growth post-2015 more broad-based, tech-driven: Paper
articles.summary: A new paper published in The Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences states India's farm sector growth averaged 4.5% since 2015, surpassing earlier phases (3%). This growth is broad-based, driven by technological innovations, sustainability emphasis, and diversification across commodities, unlike the Green Revolution's cereal focus. It calls for aligning incentives with resource conservation.

articles.headline: Import duty on edible oils cut to check food inflation
articles.summary: The Centre cut import duties on crude palm and soyoil from 10% to 5%, and refined oils from 32.5% to 27.5%, effective Thursday. Crude sunflower oil duty is now 0%, refined at 22.5%. These cuts aim to curb food inflation, which saw wholesale price index-based food inflation rise to a 20-month high of 7.1% in August.

articles.headline: Indian Rlys’ coach overhaul on track for completion in FY28
articles.summary: The Ministry of Railways aims to complete converting all existing Integral Coach Factory (ICF) coaches on mail/express trains to Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches by FY28. Roughly 340-350 rakes remain. The move enhances safety and efficiency, with Amrit Bharat push-pull trains featuring LHB coaches and offering safer, faster operations.

articles.headline: Irdai proposes tighter expense limits for insurers
articles.summary: Irdai proposed a phased reduction in Expense of Management (EoM) limits for insurers, aiming to lower insurance costs and expand risk pools. Life insurers must cut EoM to 15% of GDPI in two years, 12.5% in five. General insurers face a cut from 30% to 20% of domestic GDPI over five years, alongside new commission caps.

articles.headline: Dolly Parton’s estate in turmoil after extortion accusations
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s longtime manager accused her nephew and former security detail, Bryan Seaver, of threats and extortion over Parton's estate. Court filings allege Seaver issued profane threats and demanded money after being fired, threatening to ruin Parton's brand. Seaver denies the claims, stating his resolve to protect her family.

articles.headline: Voltas eyeing growth over margins in near term
articles.summary: White goods manufacturer Voltas is prioritizing market share and absolute operating profit over near-term margins. The company aims for strong growth in room ACs and high-growth areas like data centers. Dealer inventory is down, but commodity prices and intense competition pose risks to margin recovery. A compressor JV with Atomberg is planned for Q4FY28.

articles.headline: NSE 4th mega IPO to alter issue size since FY05
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO, set to list Thursday, is the fourth mega IPO (~5,000 crore) to adjust its issue size since FY05. With a planned mop-up of ~22,568.94 crore, the NSE cut its offered shares by 15.09%. Historically, only one of the three prior mega IPOs (Reliance Power, LIC, ICICI Prudential AMC) saw its shares close above issue price.

articles.headline: Sebi plans review of merchant banking rules, IPO cost structure
articles.summary: Sebi is set to review merchant banking regulations and overhaul the public issue framework to simplify processes, reduce compliance, and lower IPO costs. A consultation paper on IPO cost structures is expected soon. The review will streamline redundant provisions and clarify roles and responsibilities for merchant bankers, reassessing valuation provisions.

articles.headline: Hindi-speaking belt emerging as new growth engine for MFs’
articles.summary: The Hindi-speaking belt is emerging as a significant growth engine for mutual funds (MFs), driven by changing household savings behavior towards financial assets and increased digital access. AMFI Vice-Chairman Vishal Kapoor emphasized financial awareness and making investment information available in Hindi and other regional languages to further penetration beyond top 30 cities.

articles.headline: Meesho shares worth ~900 cr change hands in mega block deal
articles.summary: Nearly ~900 crore worth of Meesho shares (0.84% stake) were sold in a block deal, following Softbank’s previous ~1,650 crore stake offloading. RPS WOS II LLC sold the shares, with Government of Singapore (~307.5 crore) and Mirae Asset Mutual Fund (~179.9 crore) being major buyers. Meesho's stock closed 1.6% lower on NSE.

articles.headline: NSE shares to also trade on MSE from Thursday
articles.summary: National Stock Exchange (NSE) shares will also trade on the Metropolitan Stock Exchange (MSE) from Thursday under the 'permitted to trade' category, according to an MSE circular. While BSE is NSE's designated stock exchange, other bourses can list its shares. NSE shares are expected to list at a ~4% premium in the grey market.

articles.headline: What to do if a lender forcibly repossesses your vehicle
articles.summary: The Supreme Court recently awarded ~10 lakh to a truck owner for unlawful vehicle repossession, criticizing RBI enforcement. If a lender repossesses a vehicle, borrowers must verify the agent's documents, ensure the repossession is peaceful and with consent, and document the vehicle's condition. Immediately dispute illegal seizures with lenders, police, or senior officers, preserving all evidence.

articles.headline: Adani Ports may sail on FY27 recovery tide
articles.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) expects a recovery in FY27, driven by capacity expansion and international growth, despite muted Q1 domestic volumes. The company targets 1 billion tonnes in volumes by 2030-31 and 17-18% annual growth in revenue and operating profit. Analysts maintain 'add' ratings, citing strong international operations and logistics ambition.

articles.headline: UPI MDR from Oct 15: Should customers switch to cards?
articles.summary: From October 15, UPI Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions above ~2,000 will incur a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), capped at ~300, paid by merchants. Customers won't pay. Small merchants (~1 lakh/month via UPI QR) and specific sectors (railways, fuel) have different or flat MDRs. Users should compare with card benefits but not blindly switch from convenient UPI.

articles.headline: Samvardhana Motherson signs MoU with Nasscom for upskilling
articles.summary: MH Supply Chain, an indirect subsidiary of Samvardhana Motherson Incorporation, signed an MoU with Nasscom to upskill its employees through the FutureSkills Prime platform. This initiative aims to enhance the skills of its workforce in new-age technologies and future-ready capabilities.

articles.headline: Jindal Stainless receives USFDA EIR with VAI status for Goa facility
articles.summary: Jindal Stainless received an Establishment Inspection Report (EIR) from the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) with a 'Voluntary Action Indicated' (VAI) status for its Goa formulations facility. This indicates minor observations that do not warrant regulatory action, allowing the company to continue operations.

articles.headline: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals inks MoU with Lubrizol for film solutions
articles.summary: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Lubrizol to develop advanced TPU-based film solutions. This partnership aims to leverage expertise from both companies to innovate in pharmaceutical packaging and delivery technologies, enhancing product stability and efficacy.

articles.headline: Setting up NSE was biggest reform in capital market: Raamdeo Agrawal
articles.summary: Raamdeo Agrawal, co-founder of Motilal Oswal Financial Services, asserts that the establishment of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in 1992 was the biggest reform in India's capital markets. He highlights its demutualized, screen-based trading, alongside dematerialized accounts (1996) and mobile internet (2004), as transformative steps, leading to increased retail participation and market capitalization.

articles.headline: Yes Bank mobilises $2 bn via FCNR(B)
articles.summary: Yes Bank mobilized ~2 billion through FCNR(B) deposits under RBI’s concessional forex swap window, using three-year and five-year maturities to replace high-cost deposits and support lending. This is part of the $133 billion mobilized by banks under the scheme. The bank will use these funds strategically, not aggressively, to match deployment needs.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank eyes digital rupee for rewards, allowances
articles.summary: HDFC Bank is developing new use cases for the RBI's central bank digital currency (CBDC), the digital rupee. These include redeeming credit card reward points for digital rupees, corporate allowances, and in-flight purchases. The bank is also integrating its CBDC wallet with BHIM for UPI-style merchant payments and planning digital rupee gift vouchers for promotions.

articles.headline: Strike may hit life insurers’ Sep biz by 10-15%
articles.summary: The three-day strike by PSU bank employees (Sep 28-30) could impact life insurers' September business by 10-15% through the bancassurance channel. The strike coincides with month-end and Q2 closing, critical for business logging. While some policies may shift to October, it will affect H1 financial year performance, as PSU banks contribute significantly to new business premium.

articles.headline: Subhash Chandra contests NCLT order restraining alienation of personal assets
