The appellate tribunal has issued notice to the CBI as proceedings continue.

articles.headline: Public sector and regional rural banks to function normally this Sunday
articles.summary: The Central government announced that all public sector banks (PSBs) and regional rural banks (RRBs) will operate normally on Sunday, September 27. The directive aims to ensure that banking needs are met ahead of a proposed three-day bank strike by certain unions starting September 28. The Finance Ministry stated that essential banking services will remain uninterrupted.

articles.headline: SEBI reviews margin requirements for longer-tenure F&O derivative contracts

articles.headline: Adani Airports plans to slash user fees by boosting non-aeronautical revenue
articles.summary: Adani Group aims to reduce passenger user fees at its eight airports to a 'bare minimum' by 2030. CEO Arun Bansal stated the strategy involves increasing non-aeronautical revenue, such as retail and real estate, to 70% of total income. The group plans a $10 billion capital expenditure to expand infrastructure and transition its airports into 'aviation hubs' with enhanced global connectivity.

articles.headline: Navitas Solar to invest ₹10,000 crore in green energy across India
articles.summary: Surat-based Navitas Solar is planning a ₹10,000-crore investment to build an integrated renewable energy ecosystem in Gujarat and Maharashtra. The project includes developing two solar parks and establishing a 2.4-GW solar module manufacturing facility. The company also plans to enter the energy storage segment with a unit in Vadodara to capitalize on India's green energy transition.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank leads Nifty 500 dividend payouts with ₹21,000 crore
articles.summary: HDFC Bank emerged as the highest dividend payer among Nifty 500 companies in FY26, distributing ₹21,000 crore. Data shows that a small group of 13 companies accounted for nearly half of the total ₹1.71-lakh crore dividends distributed. Public sector units dominated the payouts, followed by banking and petroleum sectors, reflecting improved asset quality and profitability in the banking space.

articles.headline: Samsung launches Galaxy S26 FE with AI features in India market
articles.summary: Samsung has introduced the Galaxy S26 FE in India, priced from ₹79,999. The device features a 6.7-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display, an Exynos 2500 chipset, and a 50MP primary camera. It includes integrated 'Galaxy AI' tools for photo editing and voice transcription. The phone marks a price increase over previous FE models, reflecting rising production costs and premium positioning.

articles.headline: Retailers report steady 10% growth in August ahead of festive season
articles.summary: Retail sales in India grew by 10% year-on-year in August 2026, according to the Retailers Association of India (RAI). The growth was led by quick service restaurants and grocery sectors. Regional analysis showed East India leading with 12% growth. The industry remains optimistic about the upcoming festive season, citing healthy consumer sentiment and stable macroeconomic conditions.

articles.headline: New e-commerce rules to restrict festive discounting for D2C brands
articles.summary: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Amendment Rules, 2026, are set to tighten regulations on festive discounts. The rules require benchmarks against the lowest price offered in the preceding 30 days, aiming to curb misleading 'strike-through' pricing. D2C brands are now forced to rethink their deep-discounting strategies and focus on more transparent pricing and disclosures.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu integrates sustainability into ₹3,000-crore climate resilience strategy
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu's State Environment Minister announced that sustainability is now a core part of the state's development strategy. The government has proposed a ₹3,000-crore budget for climate resilience, focusing on coastal protection, green infrastructure, and renewable energy. The state aims to meet 50% of its electricity needs through solar and wind power by 2030.

articles.headline: OECD warns global inflation may linger despite interest rate hikes
articles.summary: The OECD has warned that global inflation could remain persistent longer than expected, particularly in the US and Australia. In its latest report, the organization expects global growth to remain modest at 3.2% for 2026. Central banks are urged to maintain a 'vigilant' stance, as underlying price pressures remain durable despite previous rounds of aggressive monetary tightening.

articles.headline: Centre despatches onions to West Bengal to cool festive season prices
articles.summary: The Union government has started despatches of onions from the price stabilization buffer to West Bengal via the 'Kanda Express.' Approximately 1,400 tonnes of onions will be sold at a retail price of ₹35 per kg in Kolkata and surrounding districts. The move is intended to provide relief to consumers and maintain price stability ahead of the Dussehra and Durga Puja festivals.

articles.headline: Supreme Court refers CEC selection panel plea to Constitution Bench
articles.summary: A Supreme Court division bench has referred a petition challenging the law for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners to the Chief Justice for consideration by a Constitution Bench. The petitioners argue that the current selection panel, which includes a Union Cabinet Minister instead of the CJI, undermines the independence of the poll body.

articles.headline: Sridhar Vembu urges India to invest in foundational AI research and development
articles.summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has called on India to focus on building foundational AI and digital public infrastructure rather than relying on global frontier models. Speaking at a conclave, Vembu expressed cynicism toward global tech giants' calls to slow AI progress, suggesting it may be a monopolization tactic. He emphasized the need for locally-owned AI to ensure long-term sovereignty.

articles.headline: Mastercard exits Pine Labs after selling 4.3% stake for ₹933 crore
articles.summary: Global payments major Mastercard has exited its investment in Indian fintech unicorn Pine Labs by selling its entire 4.31% stake for ₹933 crore. The stake was sold through multiple block deals on the Bombay Stock Exchange at an average price of ₹197.75 per share. Buyers included several domestic and international mutual funds and investment firms like Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.

articles.headline: Global Institutions Raise India GDP Forecasts on Strong Demand, Investment
articles.summary: ADB, OECD, S&P Global, and Fitch Ratings have upgraded India's FY27 GDP growth forecasts, citing robust domestic demand, higher investments, and improved export performance. The OECD now projects 7.1%, making India the fastest-growing major economy. Risks include geopolitical uncertainty and El Niño.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Plans AGM in a Month, likely to Tap NCLT
articles.summary: Tata Sons plans its AGM soon to address pending corporate matters like N Chandrasekaran's reappointment, potentially approaching NCLT for directions due to a quorum issue caused by restrictions on Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT). This aims to expedite decisions amidst the ongoing dispute over trusts' shareholder rights.

articles.headline: GST Cut Lifts Entry Cars, SUVs Still Riding High
articles.summary: A year after passenger vehicle tax cuts, entry-level small car sales saw a marginal uptick, but SUV demand remains strong, securing 58% market share in FY27. The broader hatchback segment is still under pressure, indicating consumers upgrade to larger vehicles.

articles.headline: SC Delivers Split Verdict on Election Commissioner Appointment Law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court delivered a split verdict on referring challenges to the 2023 law for appointing Election Commissioners to a larger Constitution bench. Justices Datta and Sharma differed on the necessity but agreed to refer the matter to the CJI for constituting a larger bench.

articles.headline: Gen Z Voting Rights on Hold Amid EC Standoff, Revision Stalled
articles.summary: Amid Election Commission divisions, crucial decisions like the annual electoral roll revision to include 18-year-olds ("Gen Z") are stalled. Lack of consensus between the CEC and two ECs has disrupted the time-sensitive exercise, affecting nearly 50 officials' ACRs and delaying voter registration for young citizens.

articles.headline: IIT-Bombay CCTV Shows Student Handing Phone to Invigilator Before Death
articles.summary: CCTV footage from IIT-Bombay's examination hall shows Sahil Wakode, a second-year student, handing an object believed to be a mobile phone to an invigilator shortly before his death. Investigators are examining footage from the exam hall and hostel to reconstruct events.

articles.headline: Zydus Life Bets on Innovation, Specialty Drugs for Next Phase Growth
articles.summary: Zydus Lifesciences is focusing on specialty medicines, complex biologics, innovative products, medical devices, and contract manufacturing for its next growth phase. MD Sharvil Patel expects significant earnings from discovery-led business post-2030 and aims for double-digit revenue growth and improved profitability.

articles.headline: NSE Debut May Not Set Street on Fire, Sparks Later
articles.summary: NSE's public debut might be modest, with grey market premiums indicating 2-5% listing gains. However, exit curbs on most large investors could crimp immediate stock supply, potentially boosting prices later. The `22,561 crore IPO, largest in 2026, was subscribed 5.71 times.

articles.headline: WhiteOak Capital Plans D-St Foray with `1,500cr IPO
articles.summary: WhiteOak Capital, founded by former Goldman Sachs executive Prashant Khemka, plans an IPO to raise up to `1,500 crore, targeting a `9,000 crore valuation. The move follows a trend of alternative investment managers tapping public markets, with the firm managing $13 billion in assets.

articles.headline: India’s Private Sector Growth Hits 3-Month High on Services, Mfg
articles.summary: India's private sector growth reached a three-month high in September due to stronger activity in manufacturing and services, despite slower export growth. The HSBC Flash India Composite PMI rose to 56.5 from 54.3 in August, with business confidence also increasing.

articles.headline: Retaining Talent Key to India’s AI Rise, Says Salesforce Exec
articles.summary: Salesforce chief digital evangelist Vala Afshar states India can become a top AI nation if it retains its engineers and founders who are increasingly moving to Silicon Valley. He calls for public-private collaboration to create local wealth and double AI unicorn count.

articles.headline: India Urges BRICS Working Groups on Tax, Revenue Stats
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman called for two new BRICS working groups to address international taxation and revenue statistics. She highlighted disproportionate transfer pricing costs for developing nations and the need for tax frameworks reflecting economic realities.

articles.headline: Poll Panel Says Differing Views Normal Part of Deliberations
articles.summary: Under fire over red flags raised by two commissioners, the ECI asserted that differing views are a normal part of deliberations and all its orders carry full legal sanction, following established statutory procedures. Every officer is authorized to suggest improvements.

articles.headline: Oppn Says ‘Will Again Push for Motion for His Removal’
articles.summary: Many Opposition parties demanded CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, vowing to revive a pending motion for his removal. Leaders like Rahul Gandhi called "vote chori" treason, while Arvind Kejriwal sought Kumar's arrest and re-election in several states.

articles.headline: Differences Among ECs Part of Democratic Deliberations, Says BJP
articles.summary: BJP defended the Election Commission, stating that differing views among ECs during deliberations, as highlighted in a media report, reflect a democratic setup. BJP spokesman Sambit Patra argued this negates Opposition claims of the poll panel being dictatorial.

articles.headline: SC Takes Suo Motu Cognisance of Patna HC’s ‘Offending Remarks’ in Rape Case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of a Patna High Court verdict that held removing a woman’s salwar and pressing her chest did not constitute attempted rape. The SC bench indicated it might set aside the HC judgment after hearing the accused.

articles.headline: SC Notice on PIL Against Gender-based Muslim Inheritance Law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on a PIL challenging gender-based differences in Muslim Personal Law inheritance rights. The plea contends that such distinctions violate constitutional equality guarantees and seeks parity between male and female heirs in intestate succession.

articles.headline: Karnataka May Challenge HC Order on SIT Probe into Job Scam
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is likely to challenge a high court order directing an SIT probe into alleged irregularities in recruiting 400 veterinary officers, stating a CID inquiry is already underway and has found no lapses.

articles.headline: Karnataka to Expand Food Safety Drive to Street Vendors
articles.summary: Karnataka's health minister UT Khader announced an expansion of food-safety enforcement and awareness to street-food vendors, focusing on hygiene, safe food handling, and cleanliness. The initiative will cover preparation, serving, ingredients, and cooking oil use.

articles.headline: Karnataka Forms SIT to Crack Down on Insurance Claim Frauds
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) with statewide police station status to probe fraudulent insurance claims. This complies with a Supreme Court directive to fast-track investigations into suspicious claims flagged by insurers.

articles.headline: Drought-hit Taluk Selection Based on Rainfall Data, Not Discretion: CM
articles.summary: CM DK Shivakumar clarified that drought declarations are based on strict statutory criteria like rainfall data and dry spells, not political discretion. He sympathized with MLA Patil's resignation over taluk exclusions but defended the objective process.

articles.headline: One in Three Leaders Women in BJP’s New State Team
articles.summary: BJP announced its new state in-charges and co-in-charges, with 21 out of 65 leaders (32%) being women, reflecting an increased accommodation of women in organizational decision-making. Smriti Irani, D Purandeswari, and Bharati Pawar are among those appointed to key roles.

articles.headline: Domestic Air Travel Loses Momentum, Traffic Falls 6.3% YoY
articles.summary: August domestic air passenger traffic fell 6.34% year-on-year to 121.26 lakh. For the first eight months of 2026, traffic was marginally below last year. Analysts warn that West Asia conflict escalation could pose downside risks to growth due to elevated fuel prices and inflation.

articles.headline: Religious Travel Dominates Local Overnight Trips in India
articles.summary: Pilgrimage and religious travel accounted for nearly half (47.7%) of domestic overnight trips in India, followed by health/medical travel (29.6%) and holidaying/leisure (22.1%), according to the Domestic Tourism Expenditure Survey. Rental transport was major in rural, train in urban areas.

articles.headline: Myntra to Create Over 26,000 Temporary Jobs for Festive Season
articles.summary: Myntra is creating more than 26,000 temporary jobs at its fulfilment centers for the festive season, up from 11,000 last year. Women will constitute a third of the workforce, with 350 roles for differently abled individuals. Flipkart plans over 250,000 direct/indirect hires.

articles.headline: Patient Safety Top Priority Amid Probe: Pfizer India on Fake Drugs
articles.summary: Pfizer India stated patient safety and product quality are its highest priorities, reacting to Karnataka FDA's action on counterfeit drugs. The company has supported the investigation, removed affected batches, and provided technical information since the matter was brought to its attention.

articles.headline: China Carmakers Grab Record European Car Market Share
articles.summary: Chinese automakers achieved a record share of Europe's car market in August, accounting for nearly 12% of total new-car sales. They are leveraging affordable hybrid vehicles, with one in four hybrid sales coming from Chinese brands, to attract buyers wary of fully electric options.

articles.headline: NHRC Steps Up Efforts to Curb Fake Drugs with Registration System
articles.summary: The NHRC recommended a centralized medicine registration system and a trace-and-track portal with dynamic QR codes to curb spurious drugs. It also proposed a uniform SOP for forensic protocols and a national database of fake medicine cases to identify offenders.

articles.headline: FSSAI Initiates Action Against 5 E-commerce Platforms
articles.summary: FSSAI initiated penal action against Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket, Flipkart India, and Zepto for alleged regulatory violations. These range from misleading food claims (e.g., Happilo, Milky Mist) to the sale/display of prohibited items like Datura fruits and seeds.

articles.headline: VCs Turn Up Heat on Premium Indian Kitchen Startups
articles.summary: Venture capital investors are backing Indian kitchen startups that offer design-led upgrades, as the $12 billion market premiumizes. Firms like Beyond Appliances, Curaa, and EDT have raised funds, reflecting consumer demand for better design, functionality, and safer materials in modern homes.

articles.headline: Vaishnaw on Semicon, AI Risks & India’s Techno-Legal Rules
articles.summary: Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw discusses India's chip-building race, the gap with China, and accountability for AI risks. He emphasizes techno-legal rules for AI, acknowledging the need for a balanced regulatory framework amidst rapid technological advancements.

articles.headline: GCCs May Trim 30k Routine Roles, Create 150k New Tech Jobs
articles.summary: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India could see 25,000-30,000 job cuts this fiscal year due to AI-led productivity gains and global headcount reductions. However, GCCs are also expected to create around 150,000 new tech roles, driven by AI-enabled models and demand.

articles.headline: RPS Ventures Sells 0.9% Stake in Meesho for `900cr
articles.summary: RPS Ventures, a fund founded by former SoftBank Vision Fund partner Kabir Misra, sold 38.6 million shares (0.9% stake) in e-commerce marketplace Meesho for `899.7 crore via block deals. Norges Bank, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley were among the buyers.

articles.headline: Anthropic Rolls Out Claude Opus 5.5 AI Model, Prepares IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, a new AI model designed for business tasks at lower cost than its Fable 5.1 offering. It generates output faster and writes more clearly, as the startup prepares for an IPO amidst competition from OpenAI and Google.

articles.headline: Enterprise AI Startup Ultraviolette Bags $85m, Intel’s Tan Invests
articles.summary: Electric motorcycle maker Ultraviolette raised $85 million in funding, led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures, with semiconductor veteran and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan investing. The capital will scale production at its Hosur facility from 50,000 to 250,000 vehicles annually.

articles.headline: EU Proposes Rules to Dismantle Addictive Tech for Children
articles.summary: The European Union proposes new rules to regulate social media, video-sharing, and AI use by children. The KIDS Act would set age-based access rules, bring AI companions under child-safety frameworks, and require platforms to build safeguards against emotional dependency.

articles.headline: Xbox Cuts 268 Jobs, Merges Many Studios, Activision to Helm Halo
articles.summary: Microsoft's Xbox video-game unit is laying off 268 employees and consolidating several studios. Call of Duty maker Activision will now oversee the next Halo title, Rare, and Age of Empires maker World’s Edge. Halo Studios will continue to operate current Halo games.

articles.headline: Amazon Pay India Revenue Up 18% in FY26, Losses Widen
articles.summary: Amazon Pay India's operating revenue increased 18.5% to `2,484.4 crore in 2025-26, but net loss widened 33% to `1,148.5 crore. Payment-processing and promotional costs accounted for nearly four-fifths of total expenses, reversing a trend of narrowing losses in previous years.

articles.headline: Bengal Inc, Time To Land on Its Feet: Reindustrialisation Requires Strategy
articles.summary: West Bengal has committed to reindustrialization, leasing land in industrial parks. However, a larger strategy involving land acquisition, industrial policy, and addressing deficits in energy, connectivity, and logistics is needed to transform "baby steps into industrial strides" and attract investors beyond political perceptions.

articles.headline: Not Great, Wall of China-US: AI Standards Deal a Worry
articles.summary: The editorial expresses concern over a potential US-China AI standards deal, fearing it could make other nations "rule-takers." It highlights US export controls and paid AI access versus China's open-source proliferation, suggesting a contest of visions where India needs to ensure its seat in rule-making.

articles.headline: Ganesha: The Remover of Obstacles and Symbol of an Integrated Being
articles.summary: The piece explores the symbolism of Ganesh as Vighnaharta, the remover of obstacles, and Vighneshvara, the lord of obstacles. It suggests that Ganesha represents wisdom to recognize and deal with challenges, embodying an integrated human being with body, mind, intellect, and spirit.

articles.headline: Why Xi & Trump Are Really Meeting: AI Supremacy Matters
articles.summary: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet due to their separate political and economic motivations. Trump seeks to avoid negative voter impact, while Xi aims to boost a sluggish economy and secure China's tech strength. AI supremacy is key for both, with barters on rare earths and tariffs expected.

articles.headline: China, US Won’t Slow Down AI Despite Risks
articles.summary: The opinion piece argues that AI development in the US and China is unlikely to slow down despite existential risk warnings. AI has already provided significant economic benefits, compensating for demographic challenges and driving a new tech rivalry between the two superpowers.

articles.headline: New Bounce in EPFO Trampoline: Wage Ceiling Increase to `25,000
articles.summary: The EPFO wage ceiling increase from `15,000 to `25,000 extends mandatory social security (EPF, EPS, EDLI) to 51 lakh more workers. This ensures essential benefits without relying on individual saving willpower, despite increasing payroll costs for employers.

articles.headline: Movie Theatres: Popcorn Cheap Again for Customer Loyalty
articles.summary: The opinion piece suggests movie theatres should sell snacks at affordable prices (e.g., popcorn for `100-150) to boost customer loyalty and attendance. Lower margins per tub could be offset by increased sales, repeat visits, and more occupied seats, making the cinematic experience more appealing.

articles.headline: MDR to Help Bring in Surplus on UPI Deals: SBI Official
articles.summary: SBI expects to recover costs and generate a surplus from the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above `2,000 from October 15. The charges will be split among banks, payment gateways, and UPI applications, with SBI gaining significantly as both an acquiring and issuing bank.

articles.headline: Moneyview Lends More, But Pays Price in Asset Quality
articles.summary: Digital lending platform Moneyview plans a `750 crore fresh issue for growth, but its asset quality has deteriorated. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio rose to 2.7% in FY26 from 0.9% in FY24. It faces regulatory risk if unsecured lending norms tighten.

articles.headline: StockGro Parent AssetGro Fintech Plans Confidential IPO Filing
articles.summary: AssetGro Fintech, operator of the StockGro research platform, is set to file confidential draft IPO papers with Sebi for a `2,000-2,500 crore initial public offering. The offering will likely include an `800 crore fresh issue and an OFS from existing shareholders.

articles.headline: Rupee Snaps 4-Day Rally on Dollar Demand, Dollar Strength
articles.summary: The rupee closed at 95.74 to a dollar, 15 paise weaker, snapping a four-day gaining streak. Rising importer demand for the greenback ahead of the quarter-end and broad-based dollar strength weighed on the local currency.

articles.headline: Global ETF Tumbles, Sets Off Warning Bells for Investors
articles.summary: Motilal Oswal Nasdaq Q50 ETF tumbled 20% for three consecutive sessions, losing 49% cumulatively, trading at a 67% premium to its NAV. This warns investors piling into international ETFs at high premiums due to RBI limits on overseas investments and demand-supply imbalance.

articles.headline: Tata Group Fight: Trustees Chart Uncharted Territory Amid Regulatory Shift
articles.summary: The widening rift between Tata Sons and philanthropic trusts over the company's listing (due to an RBI directive) puts individual trustees under scrutiny. This unfamiliar territory challenges decades of consensus, making positions on governance and the future role of trustees increasingly significant.

articles.headline: India’s Wind Sector on Track for 100 GW by 2030: Suzlon
articles.summary: India's wind energy industry has visibility for 85 GW capacity by 2030, broadly on track for the 100 GW target. Suzlon co-founder Girish Tanti highlighted grid readiness and bidding continuity as key challenges, with the industry preparing for European expansion.

articles.headline: IBBI Gives Liquidators Leeway to Update Stakeholder Lists Independently
articles.summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) now allows liquidators to modify entries in stakeholder lists without prior adjudicating authority approval, when new information emerges. Liquidators must inform the authority within 30 days, providing greater flexibility in the liquidation process.

articles.headline: TDS Norms Eased for Banks Buying NRI Property
articles.summary: CBDT eased TDS compliance for resident individuals and HUFs buying immovable property from non-residents. Buyers no longer need a separate TAN for such transactions, allowing deposit and reporting via a PAN-based challan-cum-statement in Form 141, effective October 1, 2026.

articles.headline: Iran President Pezeshkian Rejects US Demands, Vows No Surrender
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, addressing the UN, rejected US demands and vowed no surrender, though he believes in diplomacy. This followed President Trump's threat to "annihilate" Iran, with indirect talks between US and Iranian officials yielding no public concessions amidst rising West Asia tensions.

articles.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent May Become Trump’s AI Czar
articles.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could become President Donald Trump’s new AI czar, according to sources. Trump plans to appoint an AI adviser and create an "AI force," despite previously downplaying AI concerns. Bessent led recent AI talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng.

articles.headline: Elon Musk Praises Xi Jinping, Tesla Shanghai Plant’s Talent
articles.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk praised Chinese President Xi Jinping as a "great leader" for China's immense prosperity and commended Tesla's Shanghai factory team as "incredibly talented, hardworking & trustworthy." His comments came ahead of Trump's summit with Xi.

articles.headline: Japan Calls for Removal of 'Enemy State' Tag at UN
articles.summary: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged the UN to remove references to Japan and Germany as "enemy states" from its charter, a classification China recently criticized Tokyo for. She highlighted a 2005 resolution for their removal and Japan's 70 years of contributions to the UN.

articles.headline: China Expels Top PLA Generals, Citing "Political Danger"
articles.summary: China's Communist Party expelled two top PLA generals, Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, for "serious discipline and law violations," stating it "eliminated a major hidden political danger" for the party and military. This promotes "purity and honour" of the military.

articles.headline: YouTube Unveils AI Tools, Shopping Features for Creators and Viewers
articles.summary: YouTube introduced new AI tools for creators, including Gemini-powered assistants for Shorts and YouTube Create, to help edit clips, trim pauses, and sync music. It also announced shopping updates and personalized viewer features at its Made on YouTube event.

articles.headline: China’s AI Stocks Fall on Probe into DeepSeek, Moonshot AI
articles.summary: Shares of Chinese AI model developers fell after reports that China's regulators opened a probe into startups DeepSeek and Moonshot AI over data security concerns. The investigation follows accusations from Anthropic PBC.

articles.headline: Macron Calls for Frontier AI Model Sans US, China
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron urged countries to collaborate on building an open-source "frontier AI model" independent of the "great powers”—US and China. He called for pooled investment and adherence to international laws over a "law of the jungle" in AI development.

articles.headline: Eurozone Business Activity Hits 3.5-Year High in September
articles.summary: Business activity in the eurozone grew at its fastest pace since April 2023, buoyed by solid expansion in services and manufacturing. The S&P chief business economist noted resilience despite rising energy prices, with the European Central Bank having raised rates twice in 2026.

articles.headline: Russia Hits Kyiv Hard Before Zelenskyy’s UNGA Address
articles.summary: Russia heavily attacked Kyiv with drones, killing two and wounding 23, hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the UN General Assembly. Black smoke rose above the city following daily Russian attacks, intensifying Ukraine's diplomatic efforts for international support.

articles.headline: UK to Rework Chagos Deal After Trump Criticism
articles.summary: Britain will rework its deal to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius and lease a US-UK military base on Diego Garcia, after US President Donald Trump branded the agreement "terrible." London paused the plans following vocal opposition from Trump, who replaced UK leader Andy Burnham.

articles.headline: India, EU to sign Free Trade Agreement on December 16
articles.summary: India and the European Union will sign a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) on December 16, following PM Modi's trips to Canada, US, and Belgium. The deal, which won't require individual EU country ratification, is expected to roll out by early 2027.

articles.headline: Delhi L-G orders safety audits for all public parks
articles.summary: L-G Taranjit Singh Sandhu directed MCD and DDA to conduct safety audits, install CCTV cameras, and step up vigilance in Delhi's public parks, following the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Astha Kunj Park.

articles.headline: LSR students march for women's safety after Astha Kunj gang rape
articles.summary: Hundreds of Lady Shri Ram College students held a 'women-only' solidarity march in Delhi demanding enhanced safety measures and to reclaim public spaces, following the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Astha Kunj Park.

articles.headline: 37 DTC drivers issued show-cause notices amid ongoing strike
articles.summary: 37 DTC drivers at Wazirabad depot received show-cause notices for obstructing operations during their strike, which began September 15 for better pay and social security. The union called for a full strike on Sept 28, while DTC mandated compulsory attendance.

articles.headline: Delhi HC seeks response on DUSU victory procession violations
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court sought replies from Delhi University and DUSU candidates regarding alleged victory processions on September 19, despite a court ban, after a plea claimed contempt of court.

articles.headline: Low inclusion claims for Delhi electoral roll amid mass deletions
articles.summary: Only 1.06 lakh inclusion applications were received during Delhi's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) against 47.56 lakh deletions, with a Sep 30 deadline. Officials may extend the deadline, but concerns remain over complex Form 6 declarations and low outreach to vulnerable groups.

articles.headline: Delhi HC issues notices for releasing dogs on court officer in Mehrauli
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court issued notices to two men for allegedly releasing dogs on a court-appointed Local Commissioner during a property inspection in Mehrauli, obstructing justice. The men must file affidavits and appear in court on November 19.

articles.headline: Bhupinder Singh Hooda ready for 'another fight', seeks voter support
articles.summary: Former Haryana CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda, 79, announced his intent to continue his political career, seeking public support in his Garhi Sampla-Kiloi constituency. He framed the choice as between "sitting silent" and "continuing to fight."

articles.headline: Arunachal Cabinet approves panel for controversial Siang dam survey
articles.summary: Amid protests, Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet approved a high-level committee to guide the pre-feasibility report survey for the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), an 11,000 MW hydroelectric project declared a national project in 2008. Villagers continue to resist the survey.

articles.headline: Two main accused in Sagar hooch tragedy arrested after encounter
articles.summary: Manish Lodhi alias Yashwant Thakur and Ashish Sahu, key accused in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar hooch tragedy (20 deaths), were arrested after an encounter. Lodhi suffered a leg injury. Total arrests in the case now stand at 39, with 52 named.

articles.headline: Delhi Cabinet approves 'DURGA' scheme for women, transgender e-autos
articles.summary: Delhi Cabinet approved the 'DURGA' scheme to allocate 1,300 pink electric autos (1,170 for women, 130 for transgender persons) to promote dignified self-employment and enhance safety in transport. Applicants must be Delhi residents, 20-40, with relevant licenses.

articles.headline: L-G withdraws cases against 20 in Leh violence of last year
articles.summary: Ladakh L-G Vinai Kumar Saxena announced the withdrawal of criminal cases against 20 individuals involved in the September 24, 2025 Leh protests over Statehood and Sixth Schedule demands, which resulted in four deaths. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk led a commemorative march.

articles.headline: TN Congress leader claims informing police of Veeramani scandal 2 years ago
articles.summary: M.P. Ranjan Kumar, TN Congress SC Dept. president, claims he informed Chennai police in Nov 2024 (should be 2024 given it's Sept 2026, so 2 years ago) about the child sexual abuse case involving R. Veeramani, contradicting police statements about recent complaints.

articles.headline: JD(U) to contest 60 Purvanchal seats in upcoming U.P. elections
articles.summary: Bihar's Janata Dal (United) announced it will contest 60 seats in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly election, focusing on Purvanchal areas with a significant Kurmi and Kushwaha voter base. Party leaders plan a meeting in Varanasi on October 25.

articles.headline: Badrinath cultural festival's 'bhajan jamming' sparks controversy
articles.summary: A two-day cultural festival near Badrinath temple in Uttarakhand, featuring loud "bhajan jamming," sparked controversy. Locals and religious leaders, including Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath, decried it as disturbing the religious atmosphere.

articles.headline: INLD targets Nuh to reclaim lost political ground
articles.summary: The Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) is shifting focus to Nuh, a Muslim-dominated Congress stronghold, for its 'Samman Diwas' rally on September 27. The party aims to capitalize on perceived disenchantment with Congress after its 2018 split.

articles.headline: R.C. Chavan's exit diminishes Maharashtra UCC draft panel credibility
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party MLA Rais Shaikh claimed former Bombay High Court Judge R.C. Chavan's resignation from Maharashtra's UCC drafting committee undermined its credibility. Shaikh demanded a minority representative on the panel and criticized the 'Yes/No' feedback format.

articles.headline: Keralam SIT to probe Pinarayi Vijayan in CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case
articles.summary: Keralam government constituted a SIT, led by ADGP Crime Branch H. Venkatesh, to probe corruption allegations against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his family, based on an Enforcement Directorate report seeking PCA charges. CM Satheesan states government has no option but to inquire.

articles.headline: Four students killed, one injured in Andhra Pradesh train accident
articles.summary: Four Intermediate students died and one sustained grievous injuries after being run over by Train No. 18117 near Tekkali, Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh. All victims were first-year students. CM Naidu expressed condolences and ordered advanced medical care for the injured.

articles.headline: Keralam Cabinet dissolves Loka Kerala Sabha, seeks alternative mechanism
articles.summary: The Keralam Cabinet decided to dissolve the Loka Kerala Sabha, an expatriate body, and replace it with a new mechanism to better benefit Keralites abroad. A sub-committee led by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has been formed.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Police use drone to track missing boy
articles.summary: Gudupalle police in Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh, used a surveillance drone to trace a missing 12-year-old boy within two hours after he left home following a quarrel over a mobile phone.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh temple installs first 'laddu ATM' for devotees
articles.summary: The Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam at Indrakeeladri, Vijayawada, installed Andhra Pradesh's first 'laddu ATM.' Devotees can now pay via UPI and collect prasadam from a self-service vending machine.

articles.headline: ₹1 lakh crore horticulture hub planned for Rayalaseema, Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu and Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will lay the stone for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub on October 2. The project, with ₹40,000 crore from Centre and ₹60,000 crore private investment, aims to boost horticulture and farm incomes.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM assures water release to Telangana for Jurala Project
articles.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar assured Telangana Ministers Jupally Krishna Rao and Vakiti Srihari that water would be released to the Jurala Project. Telangana, facing drought, thanked Karnataka for responding to its request amid declining water levels due to El Niño.

articles.headline: Election Commission defends decisions amid internal dissent reports
articles.summary: The Election Commission stated all its actions, including the ongoing SIR, are unanimous and legally sanctioned, following "standard administrative practice." It dismissed reports of ECs' differing views as "only one part of the picture" of deliberations.

articles.headline: Former CECs demand EC disclose details of unanimous or majority decisions
articles.summary: Former Election Commissioners urged the poll body to disclose details of its decisions, including whether they were unanimous or by majority, following reports of internal dissent. O.P. Rawat stated ECs should go public if they perceive wrongdoing.

articles.headline: BJP defends EC communications as sign of democratic functioning
articles.summary: The BJP argued that communications between the CEC and ECs, seen by Opposition as dissent, instead demonstrate democratic functioning. BJP MP Sambit Patra accused Congress of creating distrust in constitutional institutions, defending the SIR's legal validity.

articles.headline: Court grants default bail to six Ukrainian nationals in NIA case
articles.summary: A New Delhi special court granted default bail to six Ukrainian nationals arrested by the NIA in March in an alleged cross-border conspiracy involving Myanmar ethnic armed groups. They were discharged from Immigration Act sections, having served 90 days in custody.

articles.headline: India rejects OIC Group's remarks on Kashmir, calls it internal matter
articles.summary: India categorically rejected the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir's remarks on Kashmir, asserting that it's an internal matter and the Union Territories are an integral part of India. India also condemned OIC's mention of India-Pakistan conflict.

articles.headline: Former CEC Quraishi: Electoral roll revision is illegal, tailored for BJP
articles.summary: Former CEC S.Y. Quraishi stated that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is illegal and needs reversal, arguing it's tailored to favour the BJP. Opposition leaders at 'The Hindu' event echoed concerns, linking SIR to delimitation and alleging disenfranchisement.

articles.headline: Congress says UCC aims for 'permanent polarisation'
articles.summary: Congress accused the Narendra Modi government of using the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) as a political tool for "permanent polarisation," not legal reform. This comes after Justice R.C. Chavan resigned from Maharashtra's UCC panel citing differences over seeking public feedback.

articles.headline: BJP reshuffles national team, appoints new State in-charges
articles.summary: BJP national president J.P. Nadda announced a reshuffle of his national office-bearers and State in-charges. Ram Madhav gained poll-bound Uttarakhand, while Anil Baluni was promoted to overall media coordinator, ahead of anticipated Cabinet reshuffle.

articles.headline: Super El Niño predicted to cause 15,800 additional heat deaths in India
articles.summary: A Climate Impact Lab report forecasts 15,800 additional heat-related deaths in India from September 2026 to February 2027 due to the current Super El Niño. India's national rainfall deficit is 15% below normal, and heat increases electricity demand.

articles.headline: SC Justice Datta defends Collegium, criticizes Centre's 'piecemeal approvals'
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta defended the Collegium system of judicial appointments as not "judges appointing judges," criticizing the Union government's "piecemeal approvals" of recommendations. He stated judiciary cannot always be at Executive's receiving end.

articles.headline: ED claims CGPSC chairperson received ₹45 lakh bribe in exam scam
articles.summary: The ED alleged former Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission (CGPSC) chairperson Taman Singh Sonwani received a ₹45 lakh bribe, disguised as CSR funding, to favor a businessman's son and daughter-in-law in the 2021 State service examination scam. Total proceeds of crime are ₹3.28 crore.

articles.headline: IIT Bombay forms panel to probe student's death by suicide
articles.summary: IIT Bombay established a 10-member committee to investigate the death by suicide of Sahil Ravindra Wakode, a second-year B.Tech student, on September 18. Police transferred the probe to the Crime Branch. Wakode was found after being caught using ChatGPT during an exam.

articles.headline: SC grants Centre more time on Class 6 third language policy relief
articles.summary: The Supreme Court granted the Union government more time to decide on sparing the current batch of Class 6 students from the three-language policy, suggesting relief from mandatory implementation until January 1, 2027.

articles.headline: SC to examine BCI's power to regulate legal education
articles.summary: The Supreme Court decided to examine the Bar Council of India's (BCI) authority to control legal education in law colleges and national universities, questioning its expertise and potential conflict of interest in regulating and establishing institutions.

articles.headline: India to study dragon fruit export potential, diversify markets
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry is studying the potential for dragon fruit export and focusing on diversifying markets for Indian tea, particularly to Oman, Joint Secretary Amit Kumar stated at the UPASI annual conference.

articles.headline: OECD forecasts India's economic growth at 7.1% in 2026-27
articles.summary: OECD raised India's growth forecast to 7.1% for 2026-27, noting that resilient domestic demand and government policies cushioned the impact of the West Asia crisis. This follows similar upward revisions from Moody's, S&P Global, and Fitch Ratings.

articles.headline: Samvriddhi receives RBI nod for online payment aggregator services
articles.summary: Samvriddhi Inclusive Growth Network Pvt. Ltd. (SIGN), a Corporate Business Correspondent, received in-principle authorization from the RBI to operate as an Online Payment Aggregator (PA-Online), aiming to offer services for merchants after final approval.

articles.headline: Indian OMCs incur ₹530 crore daily losses on fuel sales
articles.summary: Indian Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) are estimated to incur daily under-recoveries of ₹530 crore, with losses of ₹8/litre on petrol, ₹9/litre on diesel, and ₹300/cylinder on domestic LPG due to rising crude oil prices and West Asia conflict, according to ICRA.

articles.headline: SEBI chief warns of blurring lines in financial markets
articles.summary: SEBI Chairperson Tuhin Kanta Pandey warned that increasing capital flows are blurring traditional boundaries between financial markets, raising the risk of shocks spreading. He called for closer coordination among regulators.

articles.headline: CPCL aims to join renewable energy growth, transition to petrochemicals
articles.summary: H. Shankar, MD of CPCL, stated the company is exploring investments in compressed bio-gas and sustainable aviation fuel, and plans to shift its refining from fossil fuels to petrochemicals. CPCL is also building green power infrastructure and targeting direct petrochemical entry in Nagapattinam.

articles.headline: TN Minister Rajeev: Sustainability needs measurable outcomes, policy support
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Environment Minister V.K. Rajeev emphasized that sustainability must translate into practical action and measurable outcomes, not just discussion. He committed policy support for green transition and highlighted TNPL's eco-friendly practices and CPCL's environmental focus.

articles.headline: Speakers urge mindset shift for CSR beyond mere compliance
articles.summary: Speakers at The Hindu Sustainability Summit 2026 called for a mindset change in Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) to focus on measurable impact beyond compliance. Rohit Kumar Agrawala of CPCL highlighted ESG as integral, suggesting metrics should focus on outcomes, not money spent.

articles.headline: Experts advocate water conservation, reuse for circular future
articles.summary: At The Hindu Sustainability Summit, P. Kannan of CPCL highlighted Chennai's water shortage driving the company's focus on reduce, reuse, recycle. Mukesh Mohan of IOCL emphasized recycling wastewater, while Rajiv Mittal (VA Tech WABAG) and Rajesh Nair (IIT Madras) discussed using seawater and geothermal energy.

articles.headline: Refinery sector must balance energy security with net-zero goals
articles.summary: Industry leaders at The Hindu Sustainability Summit discussed balancing energy demand and security with net-zero emissions. S.G. Venkatesh (CPCL) detailed reducing energy use and shifting to cleaner sources, while Nandakumar Velayudhan Pillai (MRPL) and Santosh K. Singh (L&T) highlighted challenges in green hydrogen and SAF.

articles.headline: CPCL General Manager: Sustainability needs action, measurable impact
articles.summary: V. Sriram, Chief General Manager, HSE, CPCL, stated at The Hindu Sustainability Summit that sustainability must move from awareness to action and measurable impact. He thanked participants and partners, emphasizing collective responsibility and partnerships for a sustainable future.

articles.headline: TN industry leaders urge incentives for green buildings
articles.summary: At The Hindu Sustainability Summit, industry leaders, including Faiza Solanki (IFC) and Navin Kumar (Navin’s), urged the Tamil Nadu government to incentivize green buildings, such as through additional FSI, to overcome customer perception of luxury and lack of understanding of benefits.

articles.headline: Start-ups need ideation-to-commercialization support for energy transition
articles.summary: Speakers at The Hindu Sustainability Summit emphasized supporting start-ups from ideation to commercialization for sustainability solutions. Indumathi M. Nambi (IIT Madras) noted a gap in incubators, while Pravin Dongre (IOCL) highlighted funding, trust, and long-term development clarity as challenges for deep tech start-ups.

articles.headline: Russia expresses interest in 'limited ceasefire', says Rubio
articles.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated Russia voiced interest in a limited ceasefire involving energy targets after talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York. However, Russia has given no public indication of agreement to such arrangements.

articles.headline: Houthis threaten U.S. interests if Saudi-led strikes supported
articles.summary: Houthi military adviser Abed Mohammed al-Thawr warned the group would attack U.S. interests in West Asia if Washington intervenes in Yemen's conflict to support Saudi Arabia or unblock the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

articles.headline: Trump-Xi truce allows China to reshape Asian order
articles.summary: As U.S. President Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping, both sides declare commitment to a "constructive relationship of strategic stability." Beijing seeks reduced U.S. interest in Asia and an Asian-led security order, advocating "Asian solutions to Asian problems" amid structural challenges and AI race.

articles.headline: U.S.-Iran shuttle talks raise hopes for West Asia peace
articles.summary: The first shuttle talks between U.S. and Iranian envoys in eight months, mediated by Qatar in New York, raised hopes for progress towards ending the West Asia war. Iran's FM spokesperson stated conditions include an end to the war and halt to U.S. "acts of aggression."

articles.headline: Pakistan shoots down 8 drones 'launched from Afghanistan'
articles.summary: Pakistan's security forces shot down eight drones allegedly launched from Afghanistan after they entered Pakistani airspace near Kohat. Afghanistan's Taliban regime denied the claims, as new border clashes add to tensions between the neighboring countries.

articles.headline: Mixed bag for India at Asian Games shooting range
articles.summary: India experienced a mixed day at the Asian Games shooting. Men's and women's skeet teams secured bronze, but individual shooters Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Raiza Dhillon finished fourth. In pistol, Manu Bhaker bowed out fifth in 10m air pistol.

articles.headline: Mirabai Chanu: 'It feels like life is complete' after Asiad silver
articles.summary: After winning Asian Games silver, Mirabai Chanu expressed profound satisfaction, saying "It feels like life is complete." She had kept her weight down to focus on the Games, missing out on previous attempts, and found the medal a culmination of years of effort.

articles.headline: Tajinderpal Toor eyes hat-trick gold as India targets 20+ athletics medals
articles.summary: Tajinderpal Singh Toor is a favourite for a third consecutive Asian Games shot-put gold. In Neeraj Chopra's absence, Rohit Yadav and Yashvir lead javelin. The 75-member athletics contingent aims for over 25 medals, hoping to improve on the previous edition's 29.

articles.headline: Gambhir: Bumrah and Hardik crucial for India in South Africa
articles.summary: Head coach Gautam Gambhir stated Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya are crucial for India's 2027 World Cup preparations in South Africa, despite their current absence (Bumrah at Asian Games, Hardik injured). He highlighted Hardik's unique ability to bowl 10 overs and bat effectively.

articles.headline: Brook, Jacks lead England to ODI victory over Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Harry Brook (67) and Will Jacks (five wickets, 46 not out) powered England to an 89-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first ODI at Chester-Le-Street, extending England's winning run after their T20I series win.

articles.headline: India open chess team wins, women outclass Germany at Olympiad
articles.summary: India's open chess team defeated England 2.5-1.5, returning to winning ways at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. The Indian women's team dominantly beat Germany 3.5-0.5, with Koneru Humpy, Divya Deshmukh, and B. Savitha Shri all winning.

articles.headline: Mohali to host India-A vs Australia-A women's red-ball game
articles.summary: The red-ball fixture between India-A women and Australia-A women, originally scheduled for Dharamshala from September 29, has been moved to Mohali due to outfield damage from the rainy season.

articles.headline: Brazil Legends beat Indian All Stars 4-3 in Kochi exhibition
articles.summary: Brazil Legends defeated Indian All Stars 4-3 in an exhibition match in Kochi, featuring former football stars like Ronaldinho and Fernandinho, who scored a hat-trick. The event, dubbed "Return of the Titans," drew a large, enthusiastic crowd.

articles.headline: Indian tennis player Parikshit Somani banned four years for doping
articles.summary: Indian tennis player Parikshit Somani has been banned for four years by the International Tennis Federation (ITF) after failing an out-of-competition drug test. The ban is effective from September 29, 2025.

articles.headline: Nihal Sarin suffers second straight loss at Chess Olympiad
articles.summary: Indian chess player Nihal Sarin suffered his second straight defeat at the Chess Olympiad, losing to Michael Adams. This comes after his previous loss to Nikita Vitiugov.

articles.headline: Sports media professional Naveen Peter passes away at 34
articles.summary: Naveen Peter, a 34-year-old sports media professional, passed away. He was digital head of a sports content company overseeing Olympics.com's India content and previously worked as a sports journalist with Deccan Herald and Deccan Chronicle.

articles.headline: Priyanshu Moliya to lead Rest of India U-23 against Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Priyanshu Moliya will captain the Rest of India U-23 team against Tamil Nadu at the JSCA Stadium in Ranchi, Jharkhand, from October 1 to 4. Angkrish Raghuvanshi is the vice-captain of the squad.

articles.headline: Anupama Ramachandran aims for billiards glory at Commonwealth Championship
articles.summary: Reigning IBSF World Snooker champion Anupama Ramachandran will represent India in English billiards at the upcoming Commonwealth Cue Sports Championship. She has been training under former Asian champion Yasin Merchant to fine-tune her technique.

articles.headline: Aronian, Abhimanyu join Total Chess pilot event
articles.summary: Levon Aronian and Abhimanyu Puranik have joined the field for the Total Chess pilot event in Chennai, conceptualized by Norway Chess and FIDE-approved. The event will take place from October 1 to 5.

articles.headline: Joshna Chinappa reflects on her record seventh Asian Games appearance
articles.summary: Squash veteran Joshna Chinappa, 40, is competing in her seventh Asian Games, an Indian record. With five Asiad medals but no gold, she discusses her longevity, training, rivalries, injury comebacks, and the sport's evolution, aiming for another medal in mixed doubles and women's team events.

articles.headline: AI's rapid math breakthroughs spark debate among scholars
articles.summary: Recent AI advancements, like Claude Fable 5 disproving the Jacobian conjecture and OpenAI solving a Millennium Prize Problem, are rapidly impacting math research. Scholars express cautious excitement, but also concern over commercial motives, lack of transparency, and AI's potential to alter the future of mathematics.

articles.headline: EAM Jaishankar raises India's concerns over US Russia sanctions bill with Rubio
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met US Senator Marco Rubio to discuss the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA). Jaishankar conveyed India's interests and concerns regarding potential 100% tariffs on Russian oil, its top supplier, and impacts on energy security and global markets. Rubio defended the bill as a tool against nations funding Russia's military.

articles.headline: Indian seaman killed in ship attack off Oman coast
articles.summary: Suraj Yadav, an Indian seafarer from Uttar Pradesh, was killed in an attack on the MV Cape Duo in the Strait of Hormuz, marking the 11th Indian casualty in the region. The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged vessel was en route from UAE to India when its engine room was targeted. Omani and Indian authorities confirmed the death.

articles.headline: Trump backs India-Middle East-Europe Corridor, urges shift from Iran
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed strong support for the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) during a meeting with the Gulf Cooperation Council. He emphasized the need to shift energy infrastructure away from Iranian checkpoints, proposing new transport routes to ensure regional energy security.

articles.headline: Man kills wife, son, priests in UP; shot dead by police
articles.summary: Arvind Singh allegedly murdered his wife, nine-year-old son, and two priests during a religious ritual in Azamgarh, UP. He then barricaded himself with his remaining children before being killed in a police encounter. One child died from injuries inflicted by Singh during the standoff.

articles.headline: Mirabai Chanu wins Asian Games silver; Jay Meena claims historic soft tennis bronze
articles.summary: Mirabai Chanu secured a silver medal in women's 49kg weightlifting at the Asian Games, ending her long wait for a podium finish. Jay Meena won India's first-ever soft tennis medal, a bronze. Indian skeet teams also won bronze medals.

articles.headline: Caribbean, Bermuda words added to Oxford English Dictionary
articles.summary: The Oxford English Dictionary has incorporated over a dozen words from Bermuda and the Caribbean, including 'bimpert' (stupid person) and 'douen' (folklore figure). These additions reflect the linguistic richness of the region.

articles.headline: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years for 2006 sexual assault
articles.summary: Disgraced movie producer Harvey Weinstein received a 15-year prison sentence in Manhattan for a 2006 sexual assault. This follows a retrial after his original 2020 conviction was overturned, marking a significant development in the #MeToo movement.

articles.headline: Congress MLA resigns over drought-hit taluk exclusion
articles.summary: Congress MLA Yashvantharayagowda Patil resigned from the Karnataka Assembly, protesting the exclusion of Indi and Chadachana taluks from the drought-hit list. Chief Minister Shivakumar clarified that declarations are based on rainfall data, not discretion.

articles.headline: Karnataka govt to challenge HC order for KPSC SIT probe
articles.summary: The Karnataka government plans to challenge the High Court's order for a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe into alleged KPSC irregularities. The government argues that internal investigations are sufficient and a court-mandated SIT is unnecessary.

articles.headline: Deep depression triggers heavy rainfall, gusty winds in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is forecast to bring heavy rainfall and gusty winds to Andhra Pradesh's coastal regions. Authorities have issued alerts, evacuated low-lying areas, and warned fishermen to stay off the sea.

articles.headline: Telangana hospital fire death toll rises to five infants
articles.summary: The death toll from a fire at the Special Neonatal Care Unit (SNCU) of RIMS Adilabad, Telangana, has risen to five infants. The blaze, suspected to be caused by a short circuit, led to the deaths of premature babies. An inquiry has been ordered.

articles.headline: SIT formed to probe corruption allegations against Vijayan, kin
articles.summary: The Kerala government has established a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate bribery and corruption allegations against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, and son-in-law concerning the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case.

articles.headline: Justice Datta: Judiciary plays 'second fiddle' to govt in judge appointments
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Datta expressed concern that the judiciary is "playing second fiddle" to the executive in judge appointments, citing government delays and selective implementation of Collegium recommendations. He stated the phrase 'judges appoint judges' is a myth.

articles.headline: SIT files charge sheet in Ram Temple donation theft case
articles.summary: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) filed a 60,000-page charge sheet against eight individuals in the Ram Temple donation theft case in Uttar Pradesh. The accused are alleged to have siphoned off crores of rupees through fraudulent means.

articles.headline: Germany ready to sign six submarine deal with India
articles.summary: Germany has signaled readiness to finalize a deal for the joint production of six submarines for the Indian Navy, valued at approximately ₹70,000 crore. The partnership involves significant technology transfer and strengthens India's 'Make in India' defense initiative.

articles.headline: NSE IPO set to debut, expected at modest premium
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is poised for its stock market debut today. Analysts predict a modest listing premium, with grey market indicators suggesting a 20% price increase. The IPO was heavily oversubscribed, reflecting strong investor confidence.

articles.headline: FSSAI penalizes Amazon, Zepto for misleading food claims
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has initiated penal action against e-commerce platforms like Amazon, BigBasket, and Zepto for misleading claims and selling prohibited items. They propose front-of-pack labels for products high in salt, sugar, or fat.

articles.headline: India men defeat England in Chess Olympiad
articles.summary: The Indian men's chess team secured a 2.5-1.5 victory against England in the Chess Olympiad, with Grandmasters R Praggnanandhaa and D Gukesh winning their matches. This win keeps India in contention for a podium finish.

articles.headline: Global agencies lift India's FY27 growth outlook to 7%
articles.summary: Fitch, S&P, and Moody's have raised India's FY27 growth forecasts to around 7%, citing economic resilience amid global conflicts and strong domestic demand. They predict RBI rate hikes due to inflation risks and rising oil prices.

articles.headline: Oil firms face ₹530 cr daily fuel losses amid surging crude prices
articles.summary: State-run oil marketing companies are incurring daily losses of approximately ₹530 crore on petrol and diesel due to a surge in crude prices and unchanged domestic fuel prices. Icra reports under-recoveries of ₹8/litre on petrol and ₹9/litre on diesel.

articles.headline: India ramps up LPG production for festive season
articles.summary: State-owned refiners have increased LPG production to nearly 44,000 tonnes daily, a 20% rise from August, to meet festive season demand. This boost comes amid supply disruptions from conflicts in the Persian Gulf.

articles.headline: Finance ministry begins pre-budget meetings on Oct 12
articles.summary: The finance ministry will commence its month-long pre-budget meetings on October 12 to finalize Revised Estimates for FY27 and Budget Estimates for FY28, preparing for the upcoming Union Budget.

articles.headline: India's business activity hits three-month high in September
articles.summary: India's private sector business activity reached a three-month high in September, with the HSBC Flash India PMI Composite Output Index rising to 56.5, driven by manufacturing and services growth.

articles.headline: Brics to establish working groups on international taxation
articles.summary: Brics countries will form two working groups focused on international taxation, transfer pricing, and revenue statistics, aiming to strengthen cooperation among tax administrations and enhance their collective voice in global tax negotiations.

articles.headline: Airtel Money plans $8-9 bn London IPO via offer for sale
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel's African fintech arm, Airtel Money, plans a London Stock Exchange listing via an offer for sale, aiming to raise $8-9 billion. No new capital will be raised; existing shareholders will sell stakes.

articles.headline: Brahma AI raises $150 mn at $2 bn valuation
articles.summary: Brahma AI, an AI-native operating system for enterprise audiovisual content, secured $150 million in funding led by Multiples, valuing the company at $2 billion. It serves global clients like Warner Bros and NBA.

articles.headline: Air India group gains market share; IndiGo slips
articles.summary: The Air India group's domestic market share rose to 26.7% in August, driven by Air India Express, while IndiGo's share dropped to 65%. Overall air traffic saw a 6.3% month-on-month decline.

articles.headline: LG, Samsung probed for alleged tariff evasion on display parts
articles.summary: India is investigating LG Electronics and Samsung for allegedly underpaying customs tariffs on imported OLED display parts for high-end TVs, claiming they wrongly used lower rates meant for older LCD/LED technology.

articles.headline: SC refers pleas against law excluding CJI from EC selection panel to larger bench
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has referred petitions challenging a 2023 law that excludes the Chief Justice of India from the Election Commissioners' selection panel to the CJI, seeking a constitution bench for adjudication.

articles.headline: Ultraviolette raises $85 mn to scale EV production, expand globally
articles.summary: Electric motorcycle maker Ultraviolette Automotive secured $85 million in funding led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures. The capital will support production scaling, new EV platform development, and international expansion, including entry into the US.

articles.headline: Banks to operate Sunday ahead of 3-day strike; salaries paid early
articles.summary: All public sector banks will open on Sunday, September 27, to mitigate disruption from a three-day strike (Sep 28-30) by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU). Government salaries and pensions will be paid early on September 25.

articles.headline: Adani family reclaims India's richest spot, surpassing Ambani
articles.summary: Gautam Adani and family have regained the top position on India's rich list, with wealth rising 13% to ₹9.23 trillion, overtaking Mukesh Ambani whose wealth fell 10%. India's billionaire count reached a record 391.

articles.headline: Karnataka to release 3 tmcft Krishna water to Telangana
articles.summary: Karnataka has agreed to release 3 tmcft of Krishna river water to Telangana in phases to protect standing crops, amidst a severe drought in Karnataka and a dispute with Tamil Nadu over Cauvery water.

articles.headline: PM Modi likely to visit Canada in December for trade pact talks
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi is expected to visit Canada in December to finalize trade agreements, including the India-Canada CEPA. Both nations aim to conclude a balanced deal that could double bilateral trade to $50 billion by 2030.

articles.headline: Pakistan curbs access to Islamabad ahead of Imran Khan march
articles.summary: Pakistan blocked major highways and deployed thousands of security forces, curbing access to Islamabad ahead of a planned march by supporters of jailed former PM Imran Khan, signaling heightened political tensions.

articles.headline: Eight Meghalaya UDP MLAs join BJP, boosting party strength
articles.summary: Eight legislators from Meghalaya's United Democratic Party (UDP) joined the BJP, increasing its strength to 10 and making it the second-largest party in the NPP-led government. The CM stated this does not disturb government functioning.

articles.headline: Opposition demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal over alleged misconduct
articles.summary: Opposition parties demand the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, citing a report of 14 formal dissents from two ECs regarding decisions made without their full knowledge, including electoral roll revisions.

articles.headline: Adani Airports CEO signals no plans to run airlines
articles.summary: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal indicated the company does not intend to compete with its airline customers, stating their focus is on airport operations. India is projected to be the fastest-growing aviation market.

articles.headline: Power lineman killed as Kuki, Naga villages attacked in Manipur
articles.summary: A 36-year-old power lineman was killed as firing on Kuki settlements and attacks on Naga villages spread across Manipur. Suspected Kuki militants attacked five Naga villages, escalating ethnic tensions and forcing residents to flee.

articles.headline: Accused in Sagar liquor tragedy injured in encounter
articles.summary: A key accused in the Sagar hooch tragedy, carrying a ₹30,000 bounty, was injured in a police encounter while attempting to escape. The accused was arrested following the exchange of fire.

articles.headline: Iran's Pezeshkian tells UN: 'We are victims of terror' by US
articles.summary: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the UN that his people have been "victims of terrorism" by the United States, displaying photos of war victims. He expressed readiness for dialogue but rejected "the language of force."

articles.headline: Four agencies raise India's FY27 growth forecast to 7%
articles.summary: ADB, OECD, S&P, and Fitch have raised India's growth forecast for the current year to approximately 7%, citing robust industrial activity, resilient domestic demand, and strong export performance.

articles.headline: IPL 2027 auction scheduled for Goa in mid-December
articles.summary: The Indian Premier League (IPL) 2027 auction is planned for December 15-16 in Goa, marking its return to India after three years. All ten franchises will participate in finalizing squads.

articles.headline: Kushagra century, Mulani's four wickets put India A in command vs Australia A
articles.summary: Kumar Kushagra scored 113 and Shams Mulani took four wickets as India 'A' took a 163-run lead over Australia 'A' in their four-day match in Puducherry.

articles.headline: India U-19 completes series sweep against Australia with six-wicket win
articles.summary: Captain Lakshya Sen scored an unbeaten 110 to lead India U-19 to a six-wicket victory over Australia U-19, completing a 3-0 clean sweep in the Youth ODI series in Rajkot.

articles.headline: India men's badminton team wins bronze at Asian Games after losing to China
articles.summary: India's men's badminton team secured a bronze medal at the Asian Games after a 1-3 semifinal loss to China. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty won their doubles match.

articles.headline: Deepika Sehrawat scores nine goals in India women's hockey 20-1 thrashing of Thailand
articles.summary: Deepika Sehrawat scored a record nine goals as India's women's hockey team defeated Thailand 20-1, securing their third consecutive Pool B victory at the Asian Games. Her tournament tally reached 20 goals.

articles.headline: Mirabai Chanu wins maiden Asian Games silver; ends medal wait
articles.summary: Mirabai Chanu secured her first Asian Games silver medal in the women's 49kg category, lifting a total of 198kg. This marks India's first weightlifting medal at the Games in 28 years.

articles.headline: India wins two skeet bronze medals at Asian Games
articles.summary: India's men's and women's skeet teams secured bronze medals at the Asian Games, providing a morale boost on a mixed day for Indian shooters. Anantjeet Singh Naruka finished fourth individually.

articles.headline: Roshibina Devi reaches wushu final, one win from gold
articles.summary: Naorem Roshibina Devi secured at least a silver medal in women's 60kg sanda at the Asian Games. She will face China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the final, aiming to become India's first wushu gold medalist.

articles.headline: FSSAI to adopt single-phase rollout for front-of-pack nutrition labels
articles.summary: FSSAI proposes a single-phase rollout for front-of-pack nutrition labelling, with red hexagon warnings for high salt, sugar, or fat. Companies will have a 365-day voluntary compliance period after regulation finalization.

articles.headline: RBI Deputy Governor sees case for rupee appreciation
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated the rupee has a fair case for appreciation due to India's economic resilience, shrinking current account deficit, and potential for a favorable capital account, despite global pressures.

articles.headline: Traders call for 'No UPI Day' on Oct 2 to protest MDR levy
articles.summary: Traders nationwide announced a 'No UPI Day' on October 2 to protest the 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions over ₹2,000, effective October 15. They argue it penalizes businesses with thin margins.

articles.headline: Subhash Chandra challenges NCLT order freezing assets
articles.summary: Zee founder Subhash Chandra appealed to the NCLAT against an NCLT order freezing his assets in personal insolvency proceedings. He disputes the bench's jurisdiction and proposes a repayment plan against admitted claims.

articles.headline: Delhi HC rejects CBI plea against ex-NSE chief Chitra Ramkrishna's bail
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court dismissed the CBI's challenge to the bail granted to former NSE MD Chitra Ramkrishna in the alleged phone interception case, finding no grounds to overturn the lower court's decision.

articles.headline: Defence Ministry orders 160 anti-airfield weapons for IAF
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed an ₹811-crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) for 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW) for the Indian Air Force, enhancing its precision strike capabilities.

articles.headline: Airtel Money files for London IPO, IFC to buy $90 mn stake
articles.summary: Airtel Money, Bharti Airtel's African fintech arm, has filed for a London IPO via an offer for sale, aiming for an $8-9 billion valuation. IFC will be a cornerstone investor, buying $90 million in shares.

articles.headline: Skipper secures ₹797 crore orders for transmission projects
articles.summary: Skipper has secured orders worth approximately ₹797 crore for transmission projects in Australia and India, bolstering its order book and contributing to its growth in the infrastructure sector.

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks reports on jail reforms and judicial backlog
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has requested reports on prison reforms, correctional facility conditions, and judicial backlog data to address case pendency and prisoner rights across the country.

articles.headline: Government to boost renewable energy infrastructure
articles.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy announced plans for significant investments in solar and wind power infrastructure to meet ambitious climate goals by 2030.

articles.headline: Health authorities monitor new COVID-19 and bird flu variants
articles.summary: Health officials are closely monitoring a new, more transmissible COVID-19 sub-variant and a new strain of avian influenza detected in poultry, with public health advisories under review.

articles.headline: India-US sign cybersecurity pact; India-France enhance nuclear cooperation
articles.summary: India and the US have signed a new agreement to boost cybersecurity cooperation through information sharing and joint exercises, while India and France have agreed to strengthen ties in nuclear energy and technology.

articles.headline: World Bank projects strong growth for India; ADB forecasts Asia's robust expansion
articles.summary: The World Bank forecasts India's economy to remain a global growth leader, citing reforms. The Asian Development Bank (ADB) predicts robust economic growth for Asia, with India being a significant contributor.

articles.headline: FSSAI plans single-phase rollout of red hexagon warning labels
articles.summary: The FSSAI proposes a single-phase rollout for front-of-pack nutrition labelling, using red hexagons to warn of high sugar, salt, or fat. A 365-day voluntary compliance period is planned after regulation finalization.

articles.headline: SC stays HC order for recovery of ₹5 lakh from Noida DM
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stayed an Allahabad High Court order for the recovery of ₹5 lakh from Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam's salary, related to the detention of a student under the National Security Act.

articles.headline: SC flags delay in disqualification case of 20 TMC rebel MPs
articles.summary: The Supreme Court flagged the delay in the Lok Sabha Speaker's decision on disqualification petitions against 20 rebel Trinamool MPs, urging expeditious resolution of the matter.

articles.headline: PM's Principal Secretary warns of global shocks, urges economic readiness
articles.summary: PK Mishra, Principal Secretary to the PM, cautioned India to prepare its economy for global shocks, citing risks from geopolitical fragmentation, import dependence, and AI development. He stressed capital mobilization and improved manufacturing.
